deckinfo.name: Yggdrasil Control
deckinfo.primer:
Hi everyone!


This is a combo/control "lands" deck that utilizes [[Elementalist]]'s passive threshold in order to play a variety of sites that help us to construct an unfair winning board-state.


The core concept is to set up a [[Sinkhole]]/[[Scorched Earth]] and [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] board reset, whilst retaining [[Bedrock]] to immediately play [[Daperyll Vampire]] or to play [[Roaming Monster]] on the Rubble that the opposing Avatar is atop.


Ideally we would have a [[Bedrock]] in play, which would allow us to immediately play a [[Daperyll Vampire]] after activating of Sinkhole or casting Scorched Earth. However oftentimes simply destroying all of our opponent's sites is more than enough to swing the game in our favor.


Thoughts after testing:


  1. Removed a [[Windmill]] for [[Gothic Tower]], the towers allows for a very smooth turn 1 Common sense fetching land surveyors for turn 2.
  2. Bottomless Pits are underperforming against our bad matchups [[Sparkmage]] and [[Battlemage]], perhaps will replace with [[Holy Ground]], [[Gnome Hollows]], [[Observatory]] or the Fire maybeboard after some testing.
  3. Sinkhole is very consistent, the full set of Scorched Earth might not be a necessity.
  4. The play experience is quite negative since the combo has very little interaction with the opponent. Not the best deck for a casual/friendly setting.



The list:


No cores?!

We are currently testing running no cores in the deck, it was observed that we seldom wanted them early as they would be destroyed during the Yggdrasil trigger, and they were also fairly poor late since we are fairly spell starved due to only drawing sites early. Might be tweaked to include a [[Ruby Core]] if we decide the Fire maybeboard is better overall post further testing.


Why all the weird ordinary singletons?

We are running 4 copies of [[Common Sense]], which allows us to have a fairly extensive toolbox for various situations and matchups, as well as to tutor up [[Lightning Bolt]] and [[Firebolts]] to end the game during Death's Door.


The Common Sense Package:

  • [[Disenchant]] - For our opponents aura's and artifacts. Particularly important against Enchantress or Battlemage.
  • [[Lightning Bolt]] - To win the game once the opponent's on Death's Door, or emergency removal in a pinch.
  • [[Firebolts]] - Same as above.
  • [[Bury]] - Generic Removal.
  • [[Land Surveyor]] - Good for blocking or for drawing towards Yggdrasil.
  • [[Apprentice Wizard]] - Just a dude that cycles a card.
  • [[Tufted Turtles]] - Our best friend against Battlemage and Sparkmage. On his shell he holds the Earth.
  • [[Roaming Monster]] - Setting up to play this immediately on your opponent's piece of rubble post wipe. Fairly potent.
  • [[Highland Clansmen]] - Finisher, kinda suspect currently, might end up being cut for [[Entangle Terrain]] for more stall.
  • [[Blizzard]] - Stalls a turn against aggro lists.


Note: Run [[Disenchant]] instead of [[Dispel]] and [[Blizzard]] instead of [[Sandstorm]] because they are more likely to be discounted off [[Philosopher's Stone]].


The essential sites:

  • [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] - The spine of the deck, our entire game-plan revolves around it and drawing into the single copy of it from our 20-card atlas.
  • [[Sinkhole]] - is the easiest way to uproot Yggdrasil, but we also have two copies of [[Scorched Earth]] as a backup in our Spellbook.
  • [[Bedrock]] - Cannot be destroyed, and way we retain a site in play post uprooting which allows us to play a minion atop it.
  • [[Crossroads]] - The best way to search our atlas for our pieces.
  • [[Pillar of Zeiros]] - A site that can singlehandedly swing the matchup against aggro in our favor post wipe.
  • [[Mirror Realm]] - Extremely flexible. It copying Crossroads allows us to potentially go through our entire Atlas looking for Yggy by turn 3.



Gameplay:


We will be drawing sites for our start of turn draws for at least the first 3-4 turns. Ideally we either have the sites we need in hand, or are playing crossroads to search for them. We also want to place a Bedrock or two down for the eventual wipe.


DO NOT just toss Roots of Yggdrasil out as a regular site.

The wipe works much better when you catch your opponent off-guard. It also leaves you open to getting blown out by [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] or [[Atlantean Fate]].

Try to innocently set a Sinkhole down and wait for your opponent to commit. Using your avatar to draw a site instead of playing a site T2/T3 is perfectly fine if you already have Yggdrasil in hand or want to set up for a [[Primordial spring]] draw early.


What if my opponent doesn't commit to the board?:

Start drawing spells after you draw a Bedrock or two, our game plan has not changed, we are still looking to wipe the board and play a minion with our remaining mana. Our opponent may have all the resources he needs in hand, but will still require a few turns to rebuild and fend off our minion.

We are now looking to use [[Craterize]] to simply One-Two punch our opponent out of the game after softening them up with attacks.


Mulligans:


Sites:

We are trying to dig for Roots of Yggdrasil, so keep [[Crossroads]] to help with that.


Priority:

Yggdrasil > crossroads > everything else.

Exception: Keep a copy of Sinkhole if you see both copies of it or Roots in your opening hand.


Spells:

[[Land Surveyor]] is our highest priority keep, followed by [[Grandmaster Wizard]], [[Common Sense]], [[Daperyll Vampire]] and [[Angel's Egg]].


Priority:

Land surveyor > Grandmaster Wizard > Common Sense = Daperyll Vampire > Angel's Egg > Everything else.


Please don't hesitate to ask any questions or to give any suggestions! The list is far from optimal and can always be improved

deckinfo.primer:
• Version 2 of the Drenched Chantress deck relies less on the jihad + small value fire minion beaters, and leans more heavily on creatures like Lord of Unland, and Ruler of Thul to pump any auras we have animated, or an army of frogs (with hammers!) Captain Baldassare presents a must-remove threat, so we don't mind drawing him early or late, and can provide great card advantage when he survives. Selfsame will let us match their big guys, don't play him early just to copy an aura if you are ahead, you might need to copy their biggest minion instead of trying to "win more" with them. Our Hydra + manuscript combo came out for 2x manticores to oppose big flyers and stay on defense since we often cast a water spell to untap him. Adept Illusionist is terrific for our bolts and explosions or getting a wildfire out as far as possible, he's good for general tenacity, but like the Captain really needs to survive for a turn to pay off, and often will prompt a preemptive removal spell from our opponent.


  • Our strategy is to spread out and diversify our angles of attack with dudes on the back line, and put out auras that disrupt our opponent in their side of the field, then close the distance either with an imperial road or over the bottom of the map with Ruler of Thul. We want to expose a minimal amount of our sites to attack in the early game, while we establish our mana pool and potential threats.


  • Strong against the earth/fire decks due to large minions being tough to bury. A geyser to animate and give flying to a large creature can be a beating.


  • One of the most important cards in the deck is probably Imperial Road. We want to be on the draw usually because we have limited card draw, and keep an eye on the opponent's hand to drop a road when they have no sites to connect the bridge across and play a silence, floor, or atlantean fate on top of their side of the battlefield.

deckinfo.name: Geomancer Ramp
deckinfo.primer:
TLDR: If you aren't replacing 3 rubbles with your [[Geomancer]] ability every game, I do not think you are correctly mulliganing OR you aren't placing your rubble in places where you can defend them with site placements in future turns. You should probably find a line where your [[Rustic Village]] makes you a foot soldier early in the game, sometimes instead of playing an [[Onyx Core]] or [[Mix Terra]] turn 1 (matchup/opening hand dependent). [[Pudge Butcher]] can win you the game with [[Earthquake]]. Don't sleep on the [[Monastery Gargoyle]] being a surprisingly resilient minion against control decks and efficient removal, especially through genesis abilities like [[Bane Widow]] and [[Death Dealer]]. (RIP to [[Bury]] effects). [[Avatar of Earth]] is currently the decks worst matchup - currently working on improving this matchup with deck changes. Where to start... comment if you have ideas!


Currently testing 1x [[Autumn Unicorn]] over 1x [[Shield Maiden]] | 1x [[Conqueror Worm]] maybe adding to top end is important since we are ramping | 1x [[Gnome Hollow]] to attempt to prevent cross board AoE Grapple Shot shenanigans - matchup is RUFF - 1x [[Scent Hounds]] in SB over [[Master Tracker]] for [[Common Sense]] synergy Kudos to @Froze for Rec!



Overall Theme: The goal of this deck is to utilize the [[Geomancer]]'s unique ability to ensure hitting our 6th site each game while drawing a spellbook card each turn to maximize early game mana efficiency by having as much information about our cards as possible and how to adapt to what we draw. In order to do this consistently, I believe your first rubble needs to be placed IN FRONT of your avatar, and on turn 2 you must always flip your top site using your [[Geomancer]]'s fill rubble unique ability. This is a standard mid-range shell, with specific minions included to help play against a few meta cards. The Deck runs a very high curve to allow top decking wars to begin to favor our deck through superior card value and never worrying about "if we can get to 7 mana this game". If piloted correctly, you will always hit your 6th land while being able to draw a spell from your spell book every turn, and with a bit of luck, have clear decision points on whether to draw from our atlas to allow us to play [[Wraetannis Titan]] | [[Craterize]] | [[Midland Army]].



Strengths:

  1. Playing to the board at all phases in a strong way
  2. Early: Ramp and Villages
  3. Mid: [[Pudge Butcher]] | [[Earthquake]] | [[Silver Valkyries]]
  4. Late: [[Wraetannis Titan]] | [[Craterize]] | [[Midland Army]]
  5. Card Advantage through [[Geomancer]]
  6. Flexible/Adaptable to opponents Deck/card draw order (few/no unwinnable matchups/early card advantage)


Weaknesses:

  1. Board Clears [[Death Dealer]] (well timed [[Monastery Gargoyle]] can help)
  2. Genesis Removal/Efficient Removal [[Bane Widow]]
  3. Reach/Burn -- Testing [[Tragedy Worrywart]] in heavy magic damage burn/reach matchups
  4. [[Infiltrate]] -- [[Master Tracker]] post-board is extremely important vs this card.
  5. Hyper Aggro - Need to play correctly, but can deal with creatureless [[Battlemage]], I think this deck is favored.
  6. [[Avatar of Earth]] - Yikes


Strategy: Ensure you are always getting three protected rubbles in each opening of the game. Prioritize stopping your opponent from being able to place lands on your rubble in the beginning turns, while drawing from your spell book each turn to maximize chances of drawing early, relevant minions to help stave off any early aggression. [[Root Spider]] played defensively along with some early villages create a safe early game to allow you to be somewhat healthy and possibly even the aggressor going into the midgame. Forcing your opponent to use early removal on your [[Pudge Butcher]] can create a strong late game.


Things to look for:

  1. [[Pudge Butcher]] and Site manipulation via [[Earthquake]] | [[Rift Valley]] | [[Atlas Wanderers]] can surprise your opponents Avatar from safe to in your clutches. This can often be a game winning tactic without a timely teleport from your opponent. This is a reason to pop an early mix if you set up butcher into site manipulation to clear a way for the projectile and drag your opponents Avatar to your [[Pudge Butcher]]. Also, sometimes, using your rift valley defensively in projectile heavy matchups, especially vs [[Flamecaller]] can be a key life conservation play.
  2. [[Crusade]] and [[Wraetannis Titan]] - reach to break through deaths door.
  3. [[Stone-gaze Gorgons]] Will disable your own minions, so be very careful in your placement, best used when you can immediately kill a problem unit via disable and then attacking it, and then repositioning your [[Stone-gaze Gorgons]] before your next attack, or saving one of your minions from [[Infiltrate]].
  4. When playing against water decks, [[Bedrock]] is a key land to help protect your units from drown effects, sometimes being correct to try and always summon minions to your [[Bedrock]] when possible, even if suboptimal position wise so that they can get some amount of value before dying if you suspect your opponent may be holding a submerge effect. This is why playing [[Bedrock]] in a centralized square [[7-9 or 12-14]] is important. Much like chess, controlling the center of the realm can be key to victory!


Things to avoid: Do not overcommit to the board and play into a board wipe if you don't need to. Forcing your opponent to keep up with your board and holding minions like [[Wraetannis Titan]] in hand for a potential [[Crusade]] combo to win post death's door can be a winning difference.


Opening hand / mulligans:

Prioritize, in no particular order:

  • Ramp | [[Älvalinne Dryads]] | [[Onyx Core]] | [[Mix Terra]] [[Frontier Settlers]]
  • Village Sites / Earth Sites

This will allow you to continue playing on curve. You almost always want to get value out of your village sites as creating a 1 power minion can create a lot of value and protect against a lot of early aggression. Block/Attack with these early and often, you will have plenty of power for the late game with the high curve.


Notable Mentions:

  • [[Stone-gaze Gorgons]] can be key to removing deathrite minions like [[Sacred Scarabs]]
  • [[Bedrock]] is very important to be under your Avatar vs water Avatar's like [[Waveshaper]] and [[Avatar of Water]]
  • [[Pillar of Zeiros]] is very important vs [[Deathspeaker]] decks
  • [[Free City]] is very good at protecting your side of the board from unwarranted aggression
  • [[Royal Bodyguard]] is best played right after being placed on deaths door
  • [[Sinkhole]] is very good if it is your first land flipped, and can be considered as played over your first rubble instead of your geomancer ability as upon activating, you will gain access to the rubble, though prioritizing an all earth hand may be more favorable in many matchups. Testing required, likely good if you can sinkhole a key threshhold land of your opponent if they have a greedy atlas.


Meta Matchups:

  • Against [[Deathspeaker]] decks, you need to compete with their early aggression. You will often be able to outvalue them within the first 9 or so turns, but if the game goes too long, their genesis triggers with recursion will prevail. Don't be afraid to get in there!
  • [[Bedrock]] is extremely strong vs control water decks and stops many of their threats from dealing you a deathblow.
  • Creatureless [[Battlemage]] deck - Meta deck Here: https://curiosa.io/decks/clk28ayqk00cql70fuy5znidf
  • You need to be willing to block vs [[Battlemage]], especially the creatureless versions. They will get card draw, it is unavoidable. Your goal is to race the [[Battlemage]] faster then they can race you. Ramp and efficient foot soldiers from sites are extra important here. Life total is key in this matchup, they will have cards, and may get stuck on lands if they aren't intentional with their card draw due to wanting to attack every turn with their [[Battlemage]]. [[Bury]] or [[Dispel]] any equipment immediately if possible. [[Wraetannis Titan]] is a great card in this matchup, and I would conisder keeping in opener if you have ramp with it. [[Dispel]] is a key side board card, and you can board out [[Root Spider]] in the creatureless matchup easily.
  • [[Enchantress]] by Zalem: https://curiosa.io/decks/clf7hjfxc002lmk0gy6nyzgl9
  • Feels like a hard matchup, after a few games of testing pre and post board, enchantress feels favored in both, [[Dispel]] makes all post-sideboard games easier, [[Rootspider]] and [[Stone-gaze Gorgons]] feel super important in this matchup, Board out [[King of the Realm]] as getting it cloned via [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] or [[Infiltrate]]d is game losing often enough, considering boarding down to 1 [[Bury]] due to many times aura's being on at least 1 water site, bricking the card. Opt for 4x [[Dispel]] and 2x [[Common Sense]] to increase chances of finding [[Dispel]].
  • [[Avatar of Earth]] This matchup is.... potentially unwinnable for this deck in its current state. May be possible post sideboard if sideboard includes [[Gnome Hollows]]. Significant revisions may be needed for the deck to compete with AoE in any meaningful way.


I exclusively (so far) play via TTS and therefor had no consideration for paper costs and have no budget version of the deck at the moment. If this deck ends up becoming strong in the meta through "sheer dumb luck" as McGonagall would say, I will do that as a fun challenge to myself. Interesting developments...

deckinfo.name: My Lovely Lady Loops
deckinfo.primer:
They massacred my boy! This deck is being workshopped as they have killed the combo via update to the Sacrifice Keyword rules text. I've got some lines cooking but idt anything will beat the OG. RIP


Magician – My Lovely Lady Loops

A hyperspeed, hidden-combo deck tech


Behold: a dirty little deck concept I’ve been cooking up that may or may not be completely unhinged.


My Lovely Lady Loops is a Magician deck built around a fully concealed, mana-conscious infinite loop that can win the game in a single turn with almost no visible setup. The entire goal of the deck is simple: Find Lady Iseult as fast as possible.


  • No midrange plans.
  • No board development.
  • Just dig, dig, dig and find that little Lady

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


The "Engine"


This deck revolves around a 4-card interaction that results in infinite Genesis triggers, executed entirely from hand without any major telegraphing.


Required Pieces in hand:


  1. Lady Iseult
  2. Moon Clan Werewolf
  3. One-shot Wizard
  4. Hamlet


The only thing that really has to be done through the game is ensuring Line-of-sight to the opposing Avatar


(Note: I added Horns to the deck as well as an alternate wincon for infinite attack dmg Loops if necessary. It's an extra piece to fish for, but at least it makes a damage reduction situation winnable)


How the Loop Works:


  1. Play Hamlet to Best Space for LOS
  2. Cast Lady Iseult (2 mana)
  3. Cast One-shot Wizard to Hamlet (Hamlet reduces the cost of Ordinary minions making Wizard cost 0 mana) --> Wizard’s Genesis deals 1 damage via projectile.
  4. Activate Moon Clan Werewolf from hand, attempting to pay its alternate cost: Sacrifice an allied Mortal (One-shot Wizard) --> Lady says "dont do that" and replaces the death with "return to hand" --> Wizard does not die and returns to hand instead
  5. Because the Wizard never actually died --> The sacrifice was never paid --> Moon Clan Werewolf is not summoned --> The game state resets to exactly where it was before Wizard was cast.
  6. Repeat indefinitely


Result:

Infinite Genesis triggers, infinite damage, mow down anything in LOS.


Why This Combo Is Especially Gross


  1. Entire combo is executed from hand
  2. Requires only one turn to DD from 100%
  3. Requires basically no prior board setup (at least nothing that cost in game resources)
  4. Costs effectively 2 mana total
  5. Can remain completely hidden until execution
  6. Opponent often gets no warning


You don’t need to telegraph anything.

You simply present lethal when the pieces line up.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


Why Magician?


Magician enables this deck to function like a combo storm deck rather than a traditional Sorcery build due to the Spellbook-only structure. Magicians replacement deck rules allow for a highly tunable site ratio build with basically no fill or fluff, just gas. Additionally, the Collection functions as an extension of the deck since the overall goal is thinning the deck and, with so Collection interaction pieces that cheaply interact with Ordinaries, it means you can play copies of core Ordinaries in your collection and have basically 7+ copies of them at your disposal.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


Deck Philosophy: Ignore the Board


This is intentionally not a creature deck and not a control deck.

Minions exist purely as mechanical components:

  • Genesis triggers
  • Spellcaster enablers
  • Sacrifice targets
  • Tutors with legs


Combat is irrelevant. Board presence is incidental.


Most games aim to end by turn 6, ideally before meaningful board states develop.


Key Support Pieces include:


Browse / Dream-Quest / Pnakotic Manuscript

Raw velocity. Life total is a resource; speed is the priority.


Wiccan Tools

Draw plus on-demand Spellcaster, enabling Dream-Quest and threshold bypass.


Toolbox + Collection

Turns Ordinary cards into functional duplicates, massively increasing combo density.


Morgana le Fay / Highland Princess

Additional digging without exposing the combo.


Sphere of Animosity & Mobility Tools

Help lock positioning and guarantee line-of-sight when it’s time to go off.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


Site Philosophy


This deck prioritizes threshold over mana.

  • Most spells are cheap so Threshold is the real bottleneck.
  • Many sites provide immediate multi-element access
  • Sites also provide utility:
  • Hamlet enables the loop
  • Elder Ruins offers a secondary sacrifice line
  • Observatory smooths the top of the deck
  • The site count is deliberate and central to consistency.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


Weaknesses (Obviously)

Ironclad (jadded an alternate wincon in Horns), and anyone that plans to move around a lot and early. mobility is ironically the greatest weakness (in a game based on mobility) hence why we are all on on hunting down our pieces. we're designed to do one thing very well and basically nothing else


That said, the deck’s speed and concealment are intended to end games before those weaknesses matter.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


In Conclusion


Is this deck good?

No idea.


Is it funny?

Absolutely.


Is it hiding a fully concealed infinite combo that wins on the spot?

Unfortunately… yes.


Edit 1: I am still workshopping the Collection to find pieces that might deal with an Ironclad situation without changing the overall identity of this deck which is balls to the wall no development, no defense, just gas and an end goal. Until then, its a scoop lol


Edit 2: I've added Horn to compensate for Ironclad issues. Now, you can play Horn before infinite casts of Wizard. Keep casting Wizard and attacking the closest site until you win.


Edit 3: Heavily considering Black Mass right now since its a "cycle 7 cards to the bottom" effect for cheap. It can find Werewolfs but thats it. Going to keep mulling it over, but considering replacing a land or a Mix maybe. Very unsure as to what goes, but this card is tempting me.

deckinfo.name: Magician Monstrosity (The Original)
deckinfo.primer:
Wanna see a magic trick?


In a world of consistent site draw, one avatar stands tall to defy them all: Enter the Magician.


The Magician captured my imagination the moment he was spoiled, as I immediately felt like there was a deck that could break him. While I have tested numerous builds and strategies, I finally settled on this deck as the one that pushes the boundaries in Sorcery: Contested Realm the hardest. Through reanimation and fast mana, the Magician aims to press its pre-game advantage to the absolute max.


Strategies:


While playing this deck, roughly 85% of games will fall into 1 of the following 3 strategies:


  • Reanimation - Utilizing Raise Dead, Boneyard, and Orpheus' Crossing, the deck is able to perform some truly insane feats as early as turn 2. Cards like Sisters of Avalon, Forgotten Tomb, and Dreadwing allow us to fill the graveyard and then reanimate way ahead of curve. Big targets include Conqueror Worm, Great Old One, Lord of the Void, and Doom of Dilmun, all of which provide unique avenues to winning the game. Raise Dead has the nifty trick of being able to summon anywhere in the realm, so placing a Conqueror Worm on your opponent's opening site demands an immediate answer or the game is essentially over.


  • Fast Mana and Big Fatties - Playing Towers, Cores, Mixes, and 4 Waters allows us to cheat things into play much earlier than expected. This gives us an advantage vs. Aggro, as our threats are much bigger and scarier than anything they can play on turns 2 or 3. Cards like Legion of Gall and Adtonitum are both disruptive and fast clocks if left unchecked.


  • Mephistopheles - For the uninitiated, this card is an absolute house. If this is in your opening hand, you immediately focus on trying to cast him as soon as possible. With a Mix or 4 Waters, a turn 2 Mephistopheles is backbreaking (assuming there is a land bridge in the realm), as he can immediately move since he replaces your avatar and avatars do not have summoning sickness. Losing the ability to play sites is trivial once you start pooping out huge threats every turn. He takes your avatar from being the worst in the game to one of the best.


It wouldn't be a Magician deck if we didn't talk about the elephant in the room. 15% of the games will likely fall into this category:


  • Mana Screw, Mana Flood, No Minions - This is the price we pay for playing the Magician. Even with 21 sites and the ability to cycle through cards via Blink, Wizard's Den, and Sisters of Avalon, a small amount of games will result in a self defeating draw. It's the price we pay for only having 60 cards in our spell book. Given the current cards in the deck, 5% of games will result in 2 or less sites being drawn.


Matchups:


One nice thing about the Magician is that its game plan is fairly consistent against any opponent. We are trying to do the same thing every game and always at the mercy of our opening hand. That said, here are some typical matchups and how we stand up against the field:


  • Aggro - As mentioned in the strategy section, aggro has a difficult time handling our threats. Most aggro strategies are running powerful 3 and 4 power threats, which are all fodder for things like Legion of Gall and Nightmare. All 3 of the strategies are solid in this matchup, just be sure not to play Orpheus' Crossing vs. any Fire list, as you are just asking to lose.


  • Midrange - Similar to the aggro matchup, we are well positioned here because our threats are typically even bigger than most mid-game threats. Cards like Root Spider and Atlantean Fate are annoying, but we have ways to fight them. Site destruction can also set them way back and really help keep the pressure on.


  • Control - Our core strategy is to utilize multiple cards to cheat minions into play. If our opponent has cheap removal (Polimorph, Disintegrate, Chains of Prometheus, etc.), we are in two-for-one hell. Landing a huge threat like Doom of Dilmun is nice here, or just pushing forward with Mephistopheles. If they have the removal, sometimes we just have to tip our hats and hope we can draw enough threats to allow us to win the game.


  • Water Necro - I still haven't figured this one out, but reanimation of Lord of the Void and Conqueror Worm are your best bets here. It's a rough matchup for sure.


Why These Cards?


There are a few head scratchers in the list, so here's a quick rundown regarding their inclusion:


  • Bane of Aventis - In any matchup with ward (which are numerous), this card is insane tempo. Permanently stealing their minion(s) can swing a game wide open and more than makes up for the fact it is a 4 power beater in some games.


  • Darkest Dungeon - This is a test card, but from what I have seen, it gives you an out to players relying on their sites to shield them from your minions. One hit and you can totally change the game from a losing one to a winning one. Potentially huge upside vs. Water Necro.


  • Sinkhole - If we are able to cheat a massive fatty in early, denying our opponent threshold and mana can essentially give us 1 or 2 free turns. This is often more than enough to win the game. It does come at the cost of threshold screw, but I believe it is worth it.


  • Den of Evil - Helps mitigate threshold screw and gives us a way of hard casting Lord of Destruction. They are often pseudo-towers, which is good utility.


  • Toolbox - Originally a 2 of, but it has become clear 3 is necessary to help push our gameplan to the absolute max. The collection is so powerful.


The Collection:


Most are self explanatory (Disenchant, Bury, Murder of Crows, Grapple Shot, Zap!), but a few are interesting tech for the deck. Common Sense allows us to find ordinary cards in our deck, which includes sites and can mitigate mana screw while also finding blink. Tactical Move is crazy movement and can setup alpha strikes to door our opponent unexpectedly or steal a site with Conqueror Worm. Dreadwing is an ordinary minion and can provide a discard outlet from the collection.


Conclusion:


The Magician can provide some of the most insane opening plays in the entire game, leaving your opponents' in awe. If that's not flavor, I don't know what is.


But it definitely comes at the risk of running completely unplayable games. If you're willing to take that risk, give this deck a shot. It is has been a labor of love and I can't wait to see where it goes from here.

deckinfo.name: Klaatu, Barada, Nektie 💀 Evil Magician
deckinfo.primer:
# The Game Plan


I once made a comment about [[Magician]] being at best no better than [[Spellslinger]]. I was way wrong. The advantage of [[Magician]] is all about the ability to see your powerful cards more often — in other words, threat density. So with that in mind, I made a deck that takes full advantage of the extra mana from (A) Air sites (i.e., [[Dark Tower]], [[Lone Tower]], [[Gothic Tower]] and [[Den of Evil]]) to make an evil deck.


I originally designed this deck to be very aggro and almost like a "Burn" or "Suicide Black" deck, if you're familiar with those Magic: The Gathering style decks; however, after playing against some of the other aggro decks in the meta, it needed to change. That is when this deck shifted into what it is today: a weird mixture of aggro and resource destruction. The new game plan seeks to play threats early and utilize them to destroy your opponent's resources to stay ahead of them. You will steal cards from their hand. You will steal minions in play. You will destroy sites. It will be fun. It will be... evil. 😈



# Notes


💀 I use [[Mix Ignis]] instead of [[Amethyst Core]] and [[Ruby Core]] and [[Philosopher's Stone]] because of [[Swap]]. I don't want to leave artifacts hanging out that can allow them to get the drop on me. Also, I designed the minion package and spells to utilize the [[Mix Ignis]] a little better. An early [[Raze]] or an early [[Lord of Destruction]] could change the entire tide of the entire game.


💀 [[Cerberus in Chains]] is great in this deck because there are a lot of times when you're unable to play or draw a site and you have nothing to do with your [[Magician]] other than move. It's also great because if you [[Blink]] your avatar, it will teleport with you. But keep in mind that it's pretty difficult to cast compared to everything else, so it may sit in your hand for a while if you draw it in the opening 7.


💀 There's a lot of demons in this deck, why not [[Demonic Contract]]? I think it's is a trap. If you think otherwise, GET IN THE COMMENTS!


💀 Remember that [[Coy Nixie]] will suffocate in the resulting [[Rubble]] after you [[Raze]], but a [[Root Spider]] will stay alive.


💀 The [[Wiccan Tools]] in the collection is there for [[Pith Imp]].



# Open Questions


❓ I'm considering [[Lord of Fear]] due to its ability to allow [[Lord of Destruction]] to attack easier. However, I just don't know if [[Lord of Fear]] is better than [[Infernal Legion]] or one of the smaller minions like [[Clamor of Harpies]], due to it raising my curve. If [[Lord of Fear]] better than [[Legion of Gall]]. Is a better curve better for the deck, or is a stronger set of minions?

deckinfo.name: Discarded Magician (Updated Primer)
deckinfo.primer:
Core Game Plan


CAUTION: This deck is more for fun than competitive


The primary objective is to rapidly fill the graveyard in order to cast large minions at a reduced cost. Threshold is largely irrelevant to this strategy; instead, minions are intentionally discarded and reanimated later for tempo advantage.

Opening Turns & Setup

Turn 1 Priorities

Ideally, open with Gothic Tower, Lone Tower, or Dark Tower, allowing you to play Sisters of Avalon. This enables an early discard of a high-impact minion, immediately setting up the graveyard.


Turn 2 Power Plays

On turn two, play Boneyard or Orpheus’ Crossing, which allows you to reanimate discarded minions as early as turn two.

If tower sites are unavailable, an alternative line is to open with Forgotten Tomb or Shallow Grave as your first site and play Cemetery Rats to begin filling the graveyard, achieving a similar setup.

If Boneyard or Orpheus’ Crossing are not drawn, the deck can instead focus on continued graveyard setup, enabling a turn three Carrionette or Raise Dead to produce the same reanimation effect.


Key Combos & Synergies

  • Discard Targets:
  • The ideal discard targets are Doom of Dilmun, Army of Undead and Infernal Legions, which can later be reanimated via Carrionette.
  • Shallow Grave / Forgotten Tomb + Boneyard/Orphues Crossing
  • This combination enables nearly any minion to be cast by turn two, with Cemetery Rats optionally played beforehand for added graveyard value.
  • Scavenging Fiend + I Am Colossus/Toolbox/Kythera Mechanism/Mix Aer
  • Provides additional combo lines and recovery options. If Mechanism is discarded unintentionally, Scavenging Fiend allows it to be retrieved.
  • Mirage
  • Improves deck consistency by replaying Shallow Grave or Forgotten Tomb, or by resetting Boneyard to generate another free minion.

Utility Staples

  • Wizard’s Den (Auto-Include)
  • Replaces itself while enabling a discard, making it ideal for fueling the graveyard. Plus positioning wont need to be defensive as we can entice our opponent to attack it.
  • Dreadwing/Sisters of Avalon allow us to discard to fill graveyard and put minions on the board.


Added Mephistopheles, because if we cheat him in with a raise dead or another we can still use his second ability/ (his first ability only works if we cast him but we don’t care about it)


this list can really have any op minion up to your discretion


Doing a little bit of tweaking, getting a tower into sisters of Avalon turn 1 is really good especially if we can discard a beefy minion, then turn 2 play a mix air, with a raise dead or carrionette allows us to play it, added another tool box and mix air

deckinfo.name: Iron Maiden - A Lesson in Inevitability
deckinfo.primer:
The Big Wigs over at Sorcery took my Lady combo out back and shot it 16 times with no warning... So, I'm bringing you a new cook thats a bit different but just as toxic. This deck and Primer is a work in progress and may see slight changes as I continue stress testing.


Iron Maiden: A Lesson in Inevitability


Deck Overview

In typical me-fashion, this deck is a "Ignore the Board and DIG" Inevitability Engine built around exploiting loss of life mechanics and Sorcery’s non-interruptive rules structure. Unlike traditional aggressive or board-centric decks, this list operates almost entirely from hand, presenting minimal telegraphing until the turn it wins.


The primary win condition leverages Iron Maiden combined with two or more Searing Truths to create a near-guaranteed checkmate scenario.


The deck is designed to:

  1. Accumulate mana rapidly
  2. Dig through the deck
  3. Sculpt its hand efficiently
  4. Withhold win-condition pieces until execution
  5. End the game decisively in a single turn cycle


Primary Win Condition: Iron Maiden + Searing Truth


Iron Maiden causes a nearby Avatar to lose life whenever they draw a card, equal to the number of cards drawn that turn.


By combining this with Searing Truth, the deck forces the opponent to:

  • Draw cards
  • Take immediate life loss from Iron Maiden for each card drawn (e.g., drawing two cards results in 2 life lost from the first draw and 3 life lost from the second, totaling 5 life)
  • Take escalating life loss from Searing Truth (which can potentially wiff, but on average should contribute additional meaningful life loss)


In practice, the deck aims to resolve at least two Searing Truths. Two Searing Truths guarantee 14 life loss through Iron Maiden triggers alone, requiring only 6 additional life loss from the spells themselves. While resolving three Searing Truths represents a fully deterministic DD guarantee, it is more mana-intensive and less common.


Because the deck runs incidental but impactful minions, it is not unlikely that additional damage or life loss has, or can, occurr prior to execution (I.e. your Greater Blood Demon is on space number 13 and swings on the Site in front of it, dealing 6 dmg as loss of life and bringing it into a hypothetical "nearby" range of the enemy Avatar). Now, you can start your combo.


With Iron Maiden + 2 Searing Truths, they will almost always be left on Death’s Door.


Importantly to Note:

  • This is loss of life, not damage, so we're bypassing most damage mitigation effects (like Ironclad)
  • It does not rely on attacks, loops, or recursion
  • Once on DD, you need to deal the final blow which we have baked into our Collection. While digging through the deck, its important to play a Silver Bullet if possible as it effectively guarantees the win on the turn following DD, by using something like Flanking Maneuver to reposition your minions for a final attack, or using a damage spell like Cone of Flame or Chain Lightning


Key factors:

  • Although you certainly can cast Iron Maiden early if you feel it necessary and, in some cases, it may benefit you to cast it a turn before you go off, Iron Maiden should typically not be cast until the winning turn in order to prevent telegraphing
  • There is no meaningful “response window” once execution begins
  • The Collection acts as an important extention of our deck. Rather than running "finishing blow" cards within the spellbook, we are reliant on either the 2 Silver Bullets, or good ole fashion combat damage.


Secondary Engines & Redundancy


Demonic Contract Package:

The deck runs a curated suite of Elite and Exceptional Demon minions specifically to enable Demonic Contract as a deterministic tutor:

  • Cerberus in Chains
  • Earl of the Ivory Towers
  • Gibbous Nightgaunts
  • Greater Blood Demon


These minions serve three roles:

  1. Enable Demonic Contract to fetch win pieces
  2. Provide legitimate board presence without telegraphing intent
  3. Act as delivery vectors to position Iron Maiden nearby the opposing Avatar


Additionally to the minions package is Brother Knight. I look at this duo as a 4-cost draw 1 attached to a 6 dmg body. I value having some extra board presence as well as the option to shuffle my deck over having just another standard 2-cost draw 1 spell.


Because the deck can run multiple copies of our main combo pieces, the combo is highly redundant and consistent. You can reasonably expect to see all of your necessary pieces by turn 6 (and hopefully earlier).


Game Plan in Phases


Early Game (Turns 1–3)

  • Develop mana aggressively through Sites and Artifacts
  • Use draw and selection spells to sculpt hand
  • Deploy minions sparingly and noncommittally
  • Plant later-game pieces as they come like Mix Ignis', Four Waters of Paradise, and Silver Bullets. These will help with both casting your final combo, and guaranteeing the finishing blow
  • The goal is to look like a slow Magician value deck... until it's not


Mid Game (Turns 4–5)

  • Continue mana development
  • Establish at least one minion capable of reaching “nearby” positioning
  • Use Demonic Contract selectively to assemble missing pieces
  • Maintain ambiguity. nothing on board should scream “combo”
  • Continue planting later-game pieces as they come like Mix Ignis', Four Waters of Paradise, and Silver Bullets.
  • At this point, the deck is typically one turn away from winning.


Execution Turn (Turns 4–6)

  • Cast Iron Maiden into a nearby space
  • Immediately follow with Searing Truth (ideally 2 copies unless their Avatars Health is already low)
  • Deal the finishing blow next turn via attack damage or a spell.


Why Board State Doesn’t Matter

  • Getting a minion within a favorable position to carry Iron Maiden is basically incidental
  • The deck doesn't care about board dominance
  • Doesn't care about life totals


Minions exist to:

  • Enable tutoring
  • Enable positioning
  • Distract opponents from the real threat (your hand)


The battlefield is a means of access, not a win condition.


Matchup Notes

Against Aggro

  • Aggro decks rarely apply enough pressure before Turn 4–5
  • Loss-of-life bypasses combat entirely
  • This forced draw concept punishes low-life strategies severely. They can accidentally put themselves in a situation where you can kill them off of just 1 Searing Truth rather than 2


Against Control

  • Control typically seems to rely on Realm interaction
  • Hand-based inevitability is more difficult to predict
  • Removal is somewhat irrelevant as minions are mostly cast as needed and are not detrimental to our plan. Removing our minions could pose some problems however, the hope is that we get to where we need to be before that really matters


Strengths

  • Extremely difficult to interact with once execution begins
  • Minimal telegraphing
  • Bypasses most defensive mechanics
  • Highly redundant combo pieces
  • Consistent win window


Weaknesses

  • Requires careful hand management
  • Vulnerable to early, unexpected life-loss pressure
  • Vulnerable to hand-hate (like discard effects)
  • Requires spatial awareness to ensure “nearby” positioning
  • Relies on the opponent not identifying the threat before it is revealed


This deck is not fast in the traditional sense. It is inevitable.


It does not overwhelm your opponent. It waits, then ends the game on its own terms.


Some Candid Thoughts

I am watching Merlin in this list like a hawk. Although we clearly run a good amount of Magic, Merlin has been leaving much to be desired for me personally. He's such a value engine, that I'm having a hard time pulling the trigger on replacing him, but he's on thin ice.


Another card that I'm considering replacing is Gibbous Nightgaunts. Not for underperformance though. This is just simply because having Elite or Unique Demons on my roster is probably more beneficial. They are staying because 3-cost, but i am strongly considering replacing with some 4-cost Elite Demons instead.

deckinfo.name: Pathfinder's Revenge
deckinfo.primer:
Backstory

After seeing a complete lack of pathfinder usage prior to April of 2023 I decided I wanted to make a deck that was fun and could work competitively against other top tier decks. After experimenting with many decks, the main consensus from people was that Pathfinder was no longer viable after being nerfed several times from the playtesting stages, so Pathfinders Revenge was born. I strove to prove Pathfinder was still able to win games while having a fun and unique mechanic to every other avatar.


Update! Rift Valley now works with Pathfinder, see FAQ entry for more info.


Strategy

The way to win with this deck is to prevent yourself from going to deaths door for as long as possible with rootspiders, divine healing, and vampires to heal lots. Then you start swinging in with the heavy hitters. Pudge can be played whenever but also remember you can use him to maneuver your own pathfinder. Highland clansmen are important because your opponent has no way to respond the turn played unless they have blockers on every site which is unlikely.



General Tips

1. You won't have the luxury to mulligan sites like every other avatar that gets the ability to see up to 6 of their sites before their first turn. For Pathfinder whatever site you get, your stuck with. To make a consistent Pathfinder deck, you need a minimum of 9 sites of each element you are playing, thus making tri-color decks very inconsistent.

2. Because of site inconsistency, don't expect to get a 2 threshold spell out until turn 3 or 4, and sometimes not even until turn 5.

3. If you start by playing two sites towards your opponent and then filling in the sites to your left or right, you are almost guaranteed to get 6 sites/mana by turn 6 every game, and at that point threshold isn't a problem anymore. To ensure more consistency or more mana, mobility spells like blink are very important

4. Unlike the sorcerer avatar you only get to draw one spell per turn and then once you're out, you're out. You need to make every spell count so adding ramp isn't as helpful, (usually) so things like cores aren't an auto include.



Mulligan

Cards You Want To See - Blink, Common Sense, Daperyll Vampire, Root Spider, Bury.

It will vary game to game, but these cards you always want to keep at least one copy of in your opening hand. Blink means you can get sites out easily while still getting a card later. Common Sense lets you get that blink you might not have drawn, or removal later in the game. Vampire and Spider both prolong you the game and are key to your victory.


Cards You Don't Want To See - Craterize, Divine Healing, Grandmaster Wizard, Lighting Bolt, Disenchant, Highland Clansmen

These you will almost always want to mulligan these in your opening hand as they will clog your hand early and you want to get those cards that will prolong the game. Craterize you want to get later in the game, and you could draw it later if you shuffle you're deck with a common sense. Divine Healing doesn't have a guarantee you can play because of 3 threshold so its a good mulligan too. There are also enough Highland Clansmen to draw one later or search one with a common sense.


Everything else you have to make an educated decision on whether or not to keep it based on other cards in hand, what avatar your opponent is playing, or just a gut feeling! Maybe you drew a Mix Aer and a Sky Baron and want to get that out early.



Match Ups

Deathspeaker: You have to be careful of wizards and vile imps beating you down since you don't have early blockers, then you go into earth fire air deathspeaker or just air fire deathspeaker which have 2 different play styles. When playing against a Deathspeaker with earth beware of Wraetannis Titan and Craterize, two power house spells that change the game very quickly. Otherwise, try to stay away from your opponents sites with your avatar and always get out of range of summoning sphere to avoid Nimbus Jinn and Vile Imps. A general tip when facing Deathspeaker would be to try not to kill their stuff so they don't get the benefit of casting it from the cemetery but also watch out for chip damage from all their little minions.


Battlemage: Very similar threat as deathspeaker, lots of early attackers could get you down to 15-10 health by turn 3 or 4 so healing from vampire or divine healing is key. Battlemage also has 2 unique play styles. For both you want to start the game by placing your second site to the left or right of your avatar to avoid them having direct access to your avatar as turn 2 grapple shot is common in these types of Battlemage aggro decks. As early as possible you need to determine if they are using minions or only artifacts and spells to buff the avatar. If they aren't using minions, take advantage of the fact that bury can target artifacts and slow down Battlemage as much as possible so you can start swinging with larger minions than they can handle.


Avatar of Earth (AoE): This match up is scary since you don't have any removal vs an avatar and you are playing earth sites which buff your opponents avatar, this avatar heavily relies on grapple shot though and pathfinder has easy mobility to avoid that while still placing sites unlike most avatars. Turn 2 site placement will vary game to game but advancing forward is an okay option as AoE doesn't a high power early on for grapple shot to be worth it. The best tip I could give in this match up is to bait their Bury and Earthquakes with weaker minions before playing a Vampire to ensure you can gain life off it, also try to play your minions on water sites if you can to prevent bury mechanics.


Sorcerer: Pretty standard avatar that could be playing a wide range of decks, the main thing you have to look out for is if you run out of cards in hand before you get them to deaths door it is basically game over since you can't survive late game vs an avatar drawing 2 spells per turn.



Didn't Make the Cut

I've tried so many variations of Pathfinder decks and discovered that many cards that work super well with almost every other deck just weren't worth playing in a Pathfinder deck. I would like to preface that you should try these out yourself and see if you come to the same conclusion because things are always changing and I'm not perfect!


Elemental cores: Overtime I found that whenever I drew an onyx core, or an amethyst core, in my games they were no longer helpful. Pathfinder ramps mana so quickly they really aren't needed and I would rather have another 5 power minions or removal. I also found mix aer to be very helpful instead because getting a heavy drop down 1 turn earlier just lets it get removed 1 turn earlier, mix aer on the other hand lets you get something down 3 turns earlier or a minion and a grapple shot in the same turn and that can be more game changing.


Philosophers Stone: I didn't hate this card and would recommend testing it yourself but I still found that since I normally get 10 sites out every game, I would rather have removal or a heavy hitter.


Frontier Settlers: With no mulling of sites you get what you get for threshold so even though these cost only 2 mana 2 earth, they commonly came down turn 3 or 4 and like I said earlier pathfinder doesn't really need more ramp but removal to kill anything your opponent ramps out.


Angel's Egg: I find it to be too slow and risky since you would in most cases play it on you avatar and Pathfinder moves around a lot, with in range of dispel, disenchant or just pushed onto opponents site. I find divine healing to be more effective at keeping me alive.


I've just taken Mirror Realm out, I don't think it works very well anymore. It doesn't help to get threshold that I don't have, just threshold that I already have so I've replaced it with a crossroads



Final Notes

This deck is very light on uniques. If you don't have a Grim Reaper feel free to swap it out for a Shield Maidens or another Skirmishers of Mu! Philosopher's Stone isn't a requirement.

deckinfo.name: Trailblazer
deckinfo.primer:
Welcome to the world of the Trailblazer!


Trailblazer [[Pathfinder]] is my version of a "Red Deck Wins" in Sorcery. While mono color Pathfinder decks tend to frowned upon due to the lack of sites needed to obtain threshold, I find that I haven't faced this issue apart from 1 game out of about 40 so far at the time of writing this.[[Ruby Core]] has been added to the list to try to help with the threshold situation as well.


Try this deck out if you enjoy aggro playstyles with lots of interactive and valuable minions, versatile burn spells, cool synergistic mechanics, and drawing spells every turn!


What this deck wants to do:


  • Play aggressively in the early game! Build towards the center of the map just about 100% of the time so that you can get your minions into action sooner (accept against Battlemage generally).
  • Burn your opponent out in the mid to late game to finish them off!
  • Trade life points for stronger board presence


What this deck does not want to do:


  • Play passively in the early game by building to the left or right of your avatar's home square (unless you are facing a Battlemage)
  • Overextend by being too greedy!



Individual card breakdown:


Minions:


[[Vile Imp]] is pretty straightforward - a 2 drop minion that deals 2 when it comes into play. Use the Genesis ability to clear out any of your opponent's minions if possible in order to make way for your units to attack! Generally speaking, I tend to not play Imp on turn two unless I have a valid target for its genesis ability.


[[Colicky Dragonettes]] - Get them into play ASAP and start chipping away at your opponent's life with them, unless you see that they have a decent minion that you could kill instead. My logic is that killing a minion that could potentially defend my attack on a future turn is more valuable than pinging my opponent for 1. Keep in mind that you can always shoot the projectile at nothing as well, don't feel like it needs to hit something if there isn't a good target!


[[Morgana le Fay]] - She is basically an unblockable 3 power minion that kind of allows you to draw three cards. Morgana is a huge removal target, so don't fixate on keeping her alive for too long. Play her when you can, draw some cards with her, prioritize playing those cards, and swing away with her in most cases. The upside of keeping her alive is that having a Stealth Spellcaster is huge in the late game, so keep that in mind!


[[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] - The best Goblins in the game! Kobolds are able to clear out smaller minions with their end of turn ability, or double the damage that they output if you can get them adjacent to the enemy avatar! Pair these with a [[Torshammar Trinket]] to push more damage!


[[Redcap Powries]] - No need to read too much into these guys. Simply a 3 drop minion with Charge is reason enough to add 3 copies of them into this list. Pathfinder is all over the board naturally, so it shouldn't be too difficult to find an advantageous angle to use them at.


[[Outback Strider]] This is just a dude on a horse that can move around the board easily. It is nice to hide away from [[Earthquake]] and [[Poison Nova]], then move up and attack during your turn. They can also move around the board to defend as well!


[[Boudicca]] - I am still deciding if the juice is worth the squeeze on this one. So many triple threshold cards can be difficult to pull off, and Boudicca doesn't do anything by herself which is another disadvantage since I like all of the minions in this list to be able to carry their own. Boudicca seems like a 'win more' kind of gal, but I'm here for it.


[[Siege Giant]] - Might seem like an odd pick at first, but they are really in here to help with potentially repositioning my Pathfinder if need be. They can also throw things like [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] & [[Colicky Dragonettes]] as well which is nice. Not to mention they can gain Charge if Rebecca is in play.


Speaking of which.....


[[Rebecks]] - I don't think there are any other 4 power minions with Charge to my knowledge [except Lion] so Rebecca makes the cut simply for being a surprise 4 damage that could also potentially give your [[Siege Giant]] Charge as well, if the odds are in your favor.


[[Clamor of Harpies]] are a cool little tech card in this deck as they can teleport your [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] over to their location as well without striking them if you need to reposition. With [[Jihad]] in play, you can also teleport and strike enemy minions with 3 or less power which is insanely impactful. They are nice against [[Avatar of Air]] since they can kill [[Palliburrie Bats]] and defend against airborne minions as well.


[[Brother Knight]] - This just seems like insane value, but we will see how they perform. BK is simply a 2 for the price of 1 type of situation, and who doesn't like that?


[[Infernal Legion]] is a huge problem that needs to be dealt with immediately. As such, you can expect to see a [[Chaos Twister]], [[Earthquake]], or other removal spell played the turn after the Legion comes into play. If possible, try to play them with a [[Magellan Globe]] or [[Jihad]] in play so that you can either drop them on your opponent's side of the board, or at the very least hit their avatar/minions with its end of turn ability with Globe.


[[Courtesan Thais]] - The best minion in this deck. Red aggro/burn decks tend to run out of steam in the late game and Thais is able to equalize that by ruining your opponent's game plan from the inside out. Knowing what decisions to make with Thais simply takes time, so the more you play with her the better you will become. My advice - try to save Thais for the turn you get you opponent to Death's Door so that you can make their avatar attack one of your minions and lose the game, if possible (sounds like a very specific plan, but the situation comes up quite often). Also, there are a lot of [[Roots of Yggdrasil]] decks running around at the time of writing this primer (June 2024). Thais can be INSANELY good against them as well. If your opponent plays a [[Sinkhole]] and passes the turn over to you, I will almost always play Thais so that I can activate [[Sinkhole]] on their turn and blow up the wrong site. I've even used 2 [[Sinkhole]]'s on an opponent while controlling their turn and they flat out conceded.


Non-Minions:


The burn spells in this deck are pretty strait forward, but I'll provide a high-level overview either way! [[Firebolts]] are mainly used to kill enemy minions, but you can also point them at your opponent's face as well if need be. If [[River of Flame]] is in play, you can use River to cast Firebolts in the subsurface at an enemy [[Root Spider]], [[Pit Vipers]], or [[Cave Troll]] as well, but that is a rare scenario.


[[Heat Ray]] typically is used as a way to finish the game once your opponent is on DD, but it can also be used to kill minions as well. I especially approve of using it to kill [[Foot Soldier]] tokens made by cards like [[Border Militia]], if everything lines up!


[[Minor Explosion]] and [[Major Explosion]] are just vanilla burn spells. Major Ex can be a real game swinging card due to how many squares it can hit simultaneously, so try to get some extra value out of it if possible. Casting Magics that care about location (i.e "up to x steps away) can be difficult with [[Pathfinder]] at times which is why I also included [[Standing Stones]] as one of the non-fire sites in this build.


[[Infiltrate]] is in an interesting place right now. A few months ago this card was in basically every Fire deck as AT LEAST a 1 of and as a result we started to see more anti-stealth tech being played in the main deck such as: [[Watchtower]], [[Scent hounds]], and [[Hounds of Ondaros]]. As a result, some players took [[Infiltrate]] out of their decks altogether. Personally, I still think that this card is amazing and I opt to run 2 of them as a result. Use these to remove enemy defenders, steal powerhouse minions, and even gain control of burrowed minions if you have [[River of flame]] in play by casting [[Infiltrate]] in the subsurface.


[[Flame wave]] usually hits your opponent for 3 damage while also killing multiple of their minions. [[Pathfinder]] especially likes this card since we can move to the edge of the realm before casting it.


[[Jihad]] is an absolute bomb in this deck. With [[Jihad]] in play, you can drop [[Vile Imp]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], [[Colicky Dragonettes]], and [[Infernal Legion]] behind enemy lines for massive value.


[[Magellan Globe]] is named after the Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan, who completed the first successful circumnavigation of the Earth in history. It seems like [[Magellan Globe]] was designed to be used by an avatar who traverses the Realm without knowledge of what lies ahead (or in this case, what Site is on top of our Atlas). This card is so so so good in [[Pathfinder]] decks in my opinion, especially this one! Being able to hit your opponent with [[Vile Imp]], [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]], [[Colicky Dragonettes]], and [[Infernal Legion]] from our side of the Realm right away is incredible. The ability to also move [[Pathfinder]] herself around the Realm with ease allows you to get extra sites in play easily while also invading your opponent's side as well.


Sites:


There aren't enough sites to support 30 Unique Fire sits at this time, so there are some seemingly odd choices of Sites in the deck at this time. Things like [[Mirage]] and [[Dwarven Forge]] are simply there to give you 1 mana and Fire threshold, that is it. [[Smokestacks of Gnaak]] have actually found themselves to be useful when they land next to an enemy site, or if you have a [[Magellan Globe]] in play which causes them to be nearby an enemy site. Generally speaking it really doesn't matter if your own Sites get shutdown due to Smokestacks, so don't worry too much about that.


The other non-Fire Sites are flexible, so feel free to swap them out. I do think that [[Standing Stones]] should stay in since they give you additional Spellcasters for your Magic spells.




Mulligan Guide:


Here are the cards that I think you should "auto-keep" in your opening hand just about 100% of the time:


  1. [[Jihad]] since it is too impactful to send away
  2. [[Courtesan Thais]] since she wins games by herself
  3. [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] and [[Colicky Dragonettes]] since they are the bread and butter of the deck - minions that beat your opponent down with abilities that push extra damage.


Here are the cards that I think you should situationally keep in your opening hand:


  1. [[Vile Imp]] should be sent back to the bottom if your opponent is playing a [Deathspeaker]]
  2. [[Magellan Globe]] if you believe that your opponent is playing an aggressive deck, such as a [[Sorcerer]] or a [[Battlemage]]
  3. [[Clamor of Harpies]] so long as your opponent isn't playing an [[Enchantress]]. This choice is totally up to you though! Harpies will not be able to teleport any of their animated Auras apart from [[Evil Spirit]], but that seldomly shows up in [[Enchantress]] deck lists.
  4. More than one burn spell should be sent back as you would always prefer to have minions in play than having burn spells in your hand. One burn spell like a [[Firebolts]] or a [[Minor Explosion]] is fine to hold on to in the beginning, but outside of that you should be sending the extras back.
  5. [[Infernal Legion]] or [[Major Explosion]] - In most cases, you don't want cards that are going to sit in your opening hand until turn 6 or 7 (or later). These cards are VERY good overall, but not ideal to find in your opening hand.

deckinfo.name: Eldritch
deckinfo.primer:
Welcome to my Eldritch themed deck!


Sorcery is probably the first CCG I’ve played that has left me really wanting to build a “themed” deck. This is aimed to scratch that itch.


For the most part this is a collection of all the “deep sea” horrors and then various support cards to try and help it run at least somewhat well.


I have recently added a splash of air (thanks for the suggestion @bleezy). I haven't played the current iteration yet but the old mono water version did have trouble with a heavy top end (it was super slow). I feel like the subtle ramp from a few towers could help as well as the extra core.


Also Air provides some significant card selection options which doesn't hurt.


A note on tactics:


This deck is very mana hungry and can be quite slow. In the early game you are probably aggressively searching for one of two things. Acceleration or a [[Porqupine Pufferfish]] with the goal of getting some kind of deterrent down to help you buy time to build.


The card draw here is spread around a bit. You have 3 [[Deep-Sea Mermaids]] which care great at getting you an expensive card you bottomed while still leaving your draw free from that spell you maybe can't cast right now. There are also a full set of [[Grandmaster Wizard]] because drawing 3 is always great, the spell caster side is mostly flavor text here however it is super useful if you do happen to find the [[Dream-Quest]]. Lastly you have [[Browse]] and [[Dream-Quest]] which while unique are great at finding what you might be looking for. The final draw path is the [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] it does require a bearer in order to draw but combined with disposable low power minions like frog tokens ([[Plague of Frogs]], [[Tadpole Pool]]) it can be a huge source of card advantage.


The real focus/strength of the deck is in card selection/filtering. Between [[Seer]], [[Fenvale Muse]] and the multitude of Ordinary Rivers you are looking at and potentially bottoming 1 to 2 cards per turn that you don't necessarily want to draw.


There isn't anything too clever going on here when it comes to finishing the game. The deck has a pretty heavy top end of big dumb beaters that will take the opponent to Death's Door in a matter of 2-3 turns from full health. It is just a matter of dodging hard removal which in some matchups can be tricky.


A note on the sideboard:


The sideboard is not super focused but more geared towards providing a bit of reinforcement when it comes to opponents who may have a more focused strategy.


Probably the the most useful/often needed in the sideboard is the [[Disenchant]] there are so many spots where it does real work. It is great against [[Enchantress]], strong against any opponent ramping with cores and or [[Philosopher’s Stone]] and also super strong against [[Battlemage]].


[[Atlantean Fate]] is probably more cute than anything. It can be very stong against any opponent playing a lot of non-basic sites. But at unique you can really rely on it too much.


[[Flanking Maneuver]] is helpful in any matchup where you may find your bodies of water broken up somehow or are trying to defend against or corral fast minions from your opponent.


[[Fey Changeling]] affords a bit more “removal” for scenarios where you are being overrun early or the opponent has minions you want to remove/disrupt but the aren’t attacking and don’t venture onto any of your water sites.


Finally there is the [[Lord of the Void]]. Which mostly carries a marginal bit of theme into the sideboard ;). Although it can be useful against opponents who are as mana hungry as this deck is.
