deckinfo.name: Ragnarök
deckinfo.primer:
"Ragnarok. The doom of the gods, man, and all things. Your time, little god, is coming to an end." -Angrboða, the Seer


Welcome to Ragnarök

This fire/earth midrange Seer deck may looks similar to many sorcerer lists that you have seen, the most popular being Fury Road. These lists thrive on efficiently costed, strong minions and capping out around 5 mana so that by turn 6 the sorcerer can use it's ability to draw 2 cards per turn and drown their opponents in card advantage.


Ragnarök similarly takes advantage of these efficiently costed minions but instead of using our avatar for advantage on turn 6 we get advantage from turn one with our scry ability.


So how do we not get drowned by card advantage starting on turn 6? Simple, we blow everything up and set our opponents back to turn 1.




This isn’t an aggro deck and it’s not your typical roots control deck. It’s a tempo deck with EF midrange as a fallback. The key here is to find roots early, pop roots around turn 5-8, drop a big minion post roots, and finish the game out before your opponent rebuilds.




How do we accomplish this?




The Gameplan



We mulligan hard for roots combo pieces. If your opener does not have 1) roots of Yggdrasil 2) sinkhole 3) bedrock, or 4) crossroads, ship it. If you have more than 1 bedrock ship the extras. You really want to get roots fast so that you've got the option to go aggressive or to hard reset if you're falling behind. (unless you know your matchup. Against Geo roots I want every bedrock I can get my hands on)




Early game you scry your atlas aggressively and bottom everything that isn't a combo piece unless you need the threshold that turn. Between your scry, mulligan, and crossroads, you are nearly guaranteed to have roots in hand by turn 7. Until I have roots/sinkhole I typically scry atlas every turn unless I know what's on top (like after a crossroads). Then once I have roots in hand I scry my spell book to sculpt my hand. I also often stop at 5 mana and tap my seer for extra sites that I'll use post roots.



There are two basic play patterns. You can either hold your minions back and prep for roots if your opponent isn't pressuring you much, or you can use your minions like you would in fury road to fight for the board / damage, all while digging for roots. If the opponent is a control deck feel free to get aggressive and push damage but dont overcommit because even against control you likely want to roots to prevent them from hitting key mana/threshold limits. Once you have Roots you can play it in your backline if you arent worried about counterplay (sinkhole, smokestacks, rift valley, Atlantean fate, Thias). Sometimes just seeing roots throws the opponent off and they stop playing to the board, in which case just kill them with your minions. If you're ever behind on board you can always pop roots. Protect your roots location with bedrocks as rift valley can be a weakness of this deck. Building your second row to a wall and dropping roots in a corner with a void between it and your avatar is perfect because it's safe from smokestacks and rift valley with your only weakness being their earthquake to bring roots off the corner or Atl fate.




The ideal time to pop roots is when you are behind on board, have at least one bedrock in play, and have a big minion in hand (Looking at you Amazon Warriors). Or if against DS or a craterize list just pop it before they hit 6-8 mana. When you pop roots you keep all of your mana for the turn (but not threshold), so ideally you pop roots, play a new land close to the opponents avatar (ideally adjacent to a forward bedrock) and drop an Amazon warrior on it. Then you have mana AND board advantage while you both recover from roots. This also has the added bonus of turning off the opposing avatar bc now it needs to tap and play sites every turn. They also often can't deal with your minion bc they are set back to 0 mana.


***** If the opponent is in earth consider just dropping roots and popping it immediately and dropping amazon warriors on your bedrock. You really dont want to play roots/sinkhole down, pass turn, then they Courtesan Thias you, or earthquake you, or Sinkhole your roots, or Craterize your roots (damn you PK). It's better to have to walk forward with your warriors a turn and lose some tempo than to get blown out.




Sometimes it's ok to roots when you're not behind on board. This is matchup dependent. If you're against a control deck or deathspeaker, you've got roots, they have 5 mana, maybe a core out, and you could pop roots and drop a minion, do it. Depriving them of that grandmaster wizard and making half the spells in their hand unplayable is completely worth it.


The other thing to mention is that sometimes you don't want to roots. This is rare but against aggro AoA or an earth fire sorcerer who actually gets more bedrocks out than you, sometimes it's correct to just try and scry your spellbook to get more quality cards to 2 for 1 them and go for an aggressive win. When to do this is hard to teach and you'll understand more with experience but if they have more bedrocks than you but are losing on board you should just push your advantage. Always think: Does popping roots here let me win? Or would waiting a turn to develop my mana/hand help me win more. Use your life total as a resource. I've won games where I was put on deaths door the turn before I pop roots, and come back to win from a 20-0 deficit.




Finally: one of the best ways to recover from roots is to recognize it early and hold your cores until post roots. As a result, if you're doing fine and can afford to take a dispel, I'll sometimes draw it (rather than bottoming it and looking for a proactive play) when against a deck that I know runs lots of cores. Popping roots, dropping an Amazon warrior, then following that up with walk up and dispel the 2 cores and P stone you held can completely devastate an opponent. Follow that up with sinkhole their only land and the game is yours.




FAQ

Why no giantesses?


-giantess is great but requires other pieces to turn it on. With our atlas being so tight we didn't have room for deserts so giantess is just unreliable




Why not play Fury road?


-you still can! I've had more success with this deck. At first no one expected roots. Now they do and it gets in their head, a lot of people don't know how to play against it. Also if they dont run bedrocks, the advantage you get from dropping a 5 power minion and resetting the game is often enough to win without a great follow up play.



Why no pudge?


I tested pudge and he isn't good against an experienced opponent. Post roots your minion needs to give you huge advantage/close out the game. Because there are rubble everywhere if you drop a pudge after roots the opponent just moves out of the way. Yes this means you get more mana advantage but you need to close the game out fast before your opponents rebuild and get card advantage and an Amazon warrior just does this so much better. Also against battlemage or Avatar of earth pudge cant block.




How does this deck do against X deck?


-I've played this deck a lot since writing the original primer above (wrote this before the online league season 4 top cut) So I feel a lot more comfortable with the matchups. The thing is that this list takes some getting used to and you play differently depending on what's across from you. Overall there are no unwinnable matchups but Geomancer roots is our hardest one. I'll try and provide some tips below.




Avatar of Air


-This used to be our hardest matchup. The high end AoA lists are easy enough, just go for roots like you would normally and save a sinkhole if you can. Always keep 2 sinkholes against AoA. The way they destroy us is by dropping bottomless pit post roots so that we cant hit them/take advantage of our tempo so you need sinkhole


-Against the Birds list by PK/Kevin, this used to be our hardest matchup. The key to winning now is to grab Smokestacks which is a new addition. We lose this match when we go for roots and dont have smokestacks bc after we pop roots they just drop a bottomless pit and we are completely stalled. With smokestacks our gameplan is back online. If you dont get smokestacks consider holding roots bc if they have the pit you really cant win. They are too low to the ground and against an experienced player they will grab extra sites so they can punish us post roots. Instead dig for sinkholes to kill their defensive sites like Bottomless pit and otherwise scry spellbook instead to grab the best minions you can. Entangled terrain/earthquake can do work, and overall our minion QUALITY is better so just scry spellbook and try and out value them with better minions.




-AoF and Aow


-Honestly I havent played these enough to give an opinion




AoE


-This is a close match but I'd say the matchup is in our favor. You still want your bedrock on your forward site to push damage when the time comes. It's also important because AoE likes to earthquake your sites closer to them so having bedrock as your forward site means they can't move it. Basically value your bedrocks higher because they may play them, use entangled terrain, quagmire, and early removal to stall them. Pop roots and hit them with amazon, usually they are easy enough to beat post roots because we basically turn off their avatar. I keep Sandworm and root spiders in this matchup to counter their root spiders




BM


-The first time you play BM you might lose, it's aggro and intimidating. But after playing this matchup a lot (Thanks Count and Jams!) I think it's actually one of our better matchups. Basically the gameplan is the same. Dig for roots, stall as best you can, dont overcommit to the board. The difference here is that BM is coming to you. It's ok to Bedrock on your first site because they are going to come up. Mull for Gnome hollows and play it one site up from your avatar. This often buys you 2 turns. Use Land surveyor as chump blockers and feel free to drop a unicorn early to get some damage in but otherwise I dont commit that much since they are coming to me and I NEED 2-3 minions for post roots. After they get to you, pop roots and drop a warrior, follow up with unicorn if possible. They cant hit you because your blockers are huge, they dont want to play sites because they are literally on top of you and are taking 5-9 damage per turn, and their removal is typically double threshold disintegrate, polymorph, or poison nova so it's often useless. Count will shrink your warrior and kill it because he's an evil genius but it's a very winnable matchup.




DS


-This is a favorable matchup as long as you can find roots. If it's one of the last 3 sites in your atlas, well that's unfortunate. Otherwise it's very much a favorable matchup. The major issue here is that they will want to hold cores and play them after you roots. Pop roots before they get 6 mana if possible, and as soon as you can if they actually get that GMW off. You dont want to die to Jinn combo. Play gnome hollows on your avatar or a root spider under you if you're not getting your combo off and they are getting a large hand. I keep dispel in my opening hand or keep a common sense around to tutor dispel if I can so I can blow up their mana rocks after roots if they play them out. Otherwise it's the same as the rest. Typically this matchup favors us.




Enchantress


-This is one of our easiest matchups actually. Root spider is protection against their enchantments, play it under a bedrock so they dont flood it. They are so reliant on high mana and threshold that roots blows them out completely. You can take a little time with this one to develop more bedrocks and a better hand before you roots typically.




Sorcerer


-This one is random because every deck is different. Basically it's the same as any matchup but you want to get multiple bedrocks so you have mana advantage post roots. They are often aggro decks so vile imps, kobolds, unicorns, removal and entangled terrain are our friends here. I've won matches by not going for roots and instead using our scry to get us better minions but I would recommend going for roots anyway. Their card advantage post turn 5 is too good. Use your Quagmires, gnome hollows, entangled terrain to stall. Get at least 2 bedrocks out, an amazon in hand (common sense is our friend here) and win with tempo. Still, they can be fast and so very variable so it's a total tossup. In general it's not easy but I'll take sorcerer over AoA any day. Also keep Bury in your opening hand because this is the deck that can randomly get a Pudge Butcher out on turn 2 and end you.




Pathfinder


-Pretty easy matchup if you play it right. They are less likely to interact with our roots combo because they dont have control over their sites. They may run Courtesan so beware of double fire threshold. They often play expensive cards so popping roots usually wins you the game. Also if they are in a corner when you pop roots you can often block them on 4-5 mana and win the game




Elemetalist


-I dont even know what a typical Elementalist deck would look like. Go for the roots plan




Geomancer


-The Geo Roots combo list from ANZ is a menace but it's beatable. I'd say it's top 3 hardest matchups for us but so many of their cards are 5+ mana that we win if we set up right. Bedrocks are the key here. Get 3-4 out (mirror realm). Dont sit on roots. If you have it you should pop it, Dont sit on it because they have plenty of ways to pop our roots and take over the game. Basically gameplan is the same, get roots, pop it when able, but dont do it unless you have at least 1 more bedrock than they do and ideally at least 2. Geo recovers from roots so well that we cant afford to pop roots with 1 bedrocks else we drown in their card advantage. Also our fire minions are excellent in this matchup bc imps and kobolds can clear their chump blockers so our fatties can get damage in. Honestly the more I play against it the more I think this is our hardest matchup.




Special thanks to PK who helped me build this list and test it against so many avatars. Your patience is unparalleled, no one else could play against this list 100 times and never complain. Also thanks to nvekmauvia Aka Kevin for many a late night of playtesting




Thanks for reading! This primer is a work in progress. Feel free to message me here or on discord with questions or thoughts and I'll get back to you as soon as I can!

deckinfo.name: The Kraken's Call (reanimator)
deckinfo.primer:
Deck Overview

Drop a big minion in the cemetery and using Raise Dead or Boneyard to bring it back into the game.


Card Choices

Seer, Browse, Dream Quest, Observatory, and Rivers can help filter through your deck to find the key cards you need to pull this off.


The non-big minions are all draw or tutor minions.


An early well placed Wizard's Den can trick opponent into attacking it allowing you to discard a large minion to reanimate the next turn.

deckinfo.name: Pool Party part 2
deckinfo.primer:
Return to the pool in Pool Party: Part 2


I built this deck mostly because I wanted a deck with big, fun monsters. There's nothing more satisfying than getting a bunch of 8-power minions out there smashing up your opponent's stuff. Just wrecking their lands and everything they love.


So how do we survive long enough to summon those big minions? The answer is simple: Sharks. Lots of sharks. [[Giant Shark]]s to be precise.


The way you play the deck is to try to mulligan for a [[Mix Aqua]] and either a [[Diluvian Kraken]] or [[Great Old One]]. No other spell is worth holding onto in your opening hand except your [[Aquamarine Core]]. For sites, the only thing you're looking for are the two [[Island Leviathan]]s. Mulligan away all other sites.


Keep using the Seer's start of turn ability on your atlas until you have both of your [[Island Leviathan]]s out. Then start digging through your spellbook for your big hitters. Those are the way you'll actually win games. Obviously use your river genesis triggers on digging through your spellbook for those big guys as well.


All the while, you'll hopefully want to draw and play all of your [[Font of Life]] right when you need them. And make sure to get a [[Giant Shark]] out into play as soon as you can. Then just sit there and make your opponent deal with it. Every turn you stall them as they figure out how to handle the shark is another turn you have to get your Leviathans (which should all be on the front row so you can alpha strike with both of them as soon as you hit 8 water affinity) and massive tentacled monsters. Make sure to use [[Riptide]] to drag your opponent into the pool and anger the shark.


Fun tips: cast Drown on your own Kraken to push it underwater so it can pop up immediately and hit everything nearby! If you draw the Pnakotic Manuscript, you can give it to a swarm of frogs to draw a bunch of cards, or you can give it to a turtle (or hydra if you're desperate) to draw a card every turn. Lastly, just hold on to an [[Ice Lance]] or, even better, a [[Rolling Boulder]] to end the game with. Neither is likely worth playing until your opponent is on death's door unless you have multiple copies clogging your hand.


So, is any of this good? Not especially. But is it fun. Do you get to have sharks, kraken, hydra, and elder gods out on the battlefield? When the stars align, yes.

deckinfo.name: Jaws/Butcher Control
deckinfo.primer:
"We're gonna need a bigger hook"

-- Jason Statham


Current Updates


8/23/2024 -- I got the combo to work for once! it was 15 points, and got hit with a Poison Nova, but I still blew off the confetti bomb. It really only works when People have a scheme in mind that doesn't pan out. There's no player that doesn't kill Pudge on-site when they know this combo is coming. Wining with rolling Boulder felt like justice considering it was a Water Avatar that could teleport anywhere.

3/15/2024 -- I really liked the addition of [[Polar Bears]] and decided to push it...and the Boulder. It's a card your opponent has to consider dealing with.


4/18/2024 -- Similar to Bears, the part where I'm forcing my opponent to play their hand earlier seems to be really effective. [[Guile Sirens]] is another card that gives opponents Hell before I start slamming down Jaws/Butcher. Now I'm also trying out some 3 mana range dudes in the form of [[Belmotte Longbowmen]]. Cards I would like to double up on are [[Torshammar Trinket]] and [[Bury]]. I'm really turning this game into a game of checkers at this point trying to make it really difficult to move around. [[Twist of Fate]] is always a feeling a bit replaceable, but the ability to just put someone on Death's Door makes it such a slammer some times.


Strategy Tips


The deck only needs 5 sites in play.


Sites to look for in your opening hand:

Mulligan aggressively for a [[Floodplain]] and a Earth site. Then start using Seer's ability to set this up if you didn't get there. The ideal set up is to put the non-water site under your Avatar, then a Floodplain in front of the Avatar. Build your sites sideways until you can get a Floodplain and some other water sites in the row above the Avatar.


Because of Giant Shark, it's important to "build a pond" in front of your Avatar and play defensively and allow to still progress your game inf the shark is in play (not often since people kill it on site). And, if Flood Plain is in front of the Avatar, you can still do upwards of 20 damage in a turn by flooding the site under your Avatar.


Spells to look for in your opening hand:

[[Pnakotic Manuscript]], [[Pudge Butcher]], [[Angel's Egg]], [[Ruler of Thule]]

Because Shark is 5 mana, it's not as important in your opening hand. Just dig for it instead.


Getting your opponents to Death's Door:

Use Seer's ability aggressively to look for Shark, Butcher, Angel's Egg, or Manuscript. Obviously use the board state to determine when to pass up cards, but I wouldn't pass the mentioned cards. [[Rolling Boulder]] is also a hard card to evaluate, but it's often a great card never to pass up.


Giant Shark + Pudge Butcher is the ideal combo. Dragging the opponents Avatar into a body of water with Shark and Pudge is usually game over. There's often not a lot of outs to move or run if this doesn't kill them. And it does happen...though not reliably enough. Often your opponent will throw everything they have to kill Pudge or Shark as soon as they're played, and you find yourself in more of a control game where your opponent is trying to figure out ways to get around them.


Remember [[Twist of Fate]] also can put your opponent at Death's Door if you're already there. Just note you won't gain the life.


Death's Door:

[[Rolling Boulder]], [[Ruler of Thule]], and [[Pudge Butcher]] are your win cons here. I guess [[Riptide]] will cause some weird scenarios too.


Synergy and Combos


[[Pudge Butcher]] + [[Giant Shark]] -- Dragging units to your water sights, shark fights, then butcher fights if it's still alive. You do 5 damage for each water site the unit gets dragged through, so you can do upwards to 20 damage in a turn...best of luck!


[[Giant Shark]] + [[Riptide]] -- Riptide has the ability to pull in units from non-water sites for the shark to fight them. If you can manage pulling in an Avatar, chaining Riptides is very deadly.


[[Pnakotic Manuscript]] + [[Tufted Turtles]] or Frog tokens -- Card advantage engine


Frog Tokens + [[Lord of Unland]] or [[Ruler of Thul]] -- just a lot of damage out of no where.


Single Card Discussion


[[Flood]] is unfortunately a necessary card in this deck. It does enable a lot of things when it works, and kills burrowing too.


[[Dispel]] while a common sense tool, is often not great. Silence effects are often welcomed against me.


[[Giant Shark]] -- This card is a little misunderstood. I'm not trying to win the game with this card by attacking my opponent. Instead, think of it more like a water board wipe. It's a card that when played, makes the game frustrating for your opponent, and often requires them to throw at least a couple of cards at it to kill it. So at it's worst, it's a 2 for 1. Another note to make about Shark in this deck is it makes Drown and similar effects a little less sought after. Shark will take out most units in the body of water, so just let your opponent deal with them!


[[Pudge Butcher]] -- Just a good card in general, and another card that gives your opponent fits.


[[Torshammar Trinket]] -- Adds power to Pudge and Shark if you're seeing bigger enemies. Also great with tokens, bears, and turtles


[[Tufted Turtles]] -- My favorite water card. This card is just very annoying for opponents to deal with. It also survives your own Shark attacks.


[[Polar Bears]] -- Their main purpose is to retrieve the Boulder, but it's also just nice to have that chip damage early in the game and apply a little bit of pressure or force removal.


[[Twist of Fate]] -- An interesting effect. [[Font of Life]] isn't too great in a multi element deck. But this card is a bit more reliable, while also attacking your opponents life. I've taken a few opponents to death's door with this card, and for that alone it's been quite useful.


[[Earthquake]] -- A card I originally hated in the deck because the amount of water, but I've really come around to learning to play with this card. The possibility of a 2 for 1 is pretty high with this card, and the ability to rearrange sites is absolutely phenomenal in this deck. Putting a Pudge on a water site, then moving it to a better position and not getting buried is a huge upside; or connecting Floodplains and water sites for Shark to be more effective is quite tricky.

deckinfo.name: ENTANGLEMAGE

Deck Tech video in the works!


Paper Sorcery gameplay of ENTANGLEMAGE can be found on my YouTube channel, On The Play;

Video 1; https://youtu.be/UJMJ7hmxRxk

Video 2; https://youtu.be/yAsTdghtf7w

Video 3; Releasing soon...


What I'm currently testing as of; 6/25/24


+1 [[Philosopher's Stone]] / -2 [[Entangle Terrain]]

  • I know, I know...dropping 2 Entangles?!...The deck is VERY focused right now and all the pieces and their quantities are very calculated. The one card I come back to as being a card that can be trimmed down is an Entangle. With 4 copies, I was seeing them a little too often and in my opener, which I don't want
  • Uncle Phil allows for playing a 3 cost minion and a Grapple in the same turn with 4 sites, as I typically stop reaching for sites once I have 4. Playing a 3 cost minion a turn can be too slow


What I'm currently testing as of; 6/23/24


+3 [[Vanguard Knights]] / -3 [[Autumn Unicorn]]

  • Playing Earth/Air and access to Tower ramp, Vanguard Knights gives me the ability to play a 4 power minion on turn 2
  • Regarding the curve of the deck, being able to cheat in a 3 drop (Bowmen, Knights, Spider) on turn 2, makes my turn 3 cleaner
  • With [[Blink]], I'm able to position the Knights to benefit from the +2 if I draw them mid game
  • Unicorn is naturally stronger but the 2 Earth threshold is clunkier than Knights
  • If I have the Bowmen, Knights, and Spider in my opener, I'm always playing the Knights first for early pressure and for positioning


+1 [[Crusade]], +1 [[Belmotte Longbowmen]], -2 [[Devil's Egg]]

  • With Crusade, there's not much that needs to be said about the +1 you get and the ability to cast minions to the affected sites. Also, being able to position a Bowmen in an Entangle to pick off the opponent Avatar
  • I decided to go with 4 Bowmen and lowering Bosk Troll to 3 because I will ALWAYS mulligan to have a Tower in my opener. So I treat all my 3 drops in the deck (which are all 1 Earth threshold) as 2 drops and use the Towers to cheat them out on turn 2. So, if I have a Bosk and Bowmen/Knight/Spider in my opener, it can be awkward for turn 2
  • With the deck being so heavy at the 3 spot and focusing on minions, I prioritize a body on the board opposed to the Egg
  • Not being able to counter an opponent's Angel's Egg is rough, which is why the Devil's Egg is in the Sideboard as this is fairly matchup dependent, like Deathspeaker or control matchups where the opponent turtles an Angel's Egg


What I'm currently testing as of; 6/20/24


+2 [[Mix Terra]] / -1 [[Onyx Core]], -1 [[Amethyst Core]] (Testing Terra vs Aer currently)

  • Entanglemage encourages splash and unsuspected damage, and the Mixes support that game style
  • The Mix is a better top deck than a single core mid/late game because with 4 sites already in play, having access to 6 mana the turn I draw a Mix mid/late game (playing it then cracking it [(4-1) + 3] has a higher ceiling than the 1 mana I'd get from a Core that doesn't even ramp me the turn it comes into play
  • Turn 2 Pudge. (RIP)
  • Testing [[Mix Aer]] with the ability to play Entangle on turn 4 then cracking an Aer and Grapple Shot across the board is very tempting. (Still testing Terra vs Aer play lines and bigger/more probable scenarios, though I'm leaning towards Terra)


+4 [[Bosk Troll]], +3 [[Belmotte Longbowmen]] (More minions!)

I originally designed the deck to have little to no minions (other than Pudge) because I wanted to make opponent's removal spells "dead cards," however, I found after countless play testing (Thanks Noah and Blake) that the deck needed additional pressure, specifically for early game presence...


Bosky boy is such a clean card in the deck in that the threshold req. is only 1 Earth and the 3 body will either;

  • Take a removal out of their hand (increased % Pudge sticks around)
  • Makes a trade with another minion
  • Kills another minion
  • Deals damage to opponent
  • "Distracts" the opponent and buys time for me to position Battlemage
  • Can put a Devil's Egg in his little troll fingers on turn 3


The Bowman is some big brain tech that I'm super proud of discovering;

  • Another clean card to cast as it's only 1 Earth threshold.
  • Turn 3 is a bit awkward for the deck, as I don't want to Grapple on turn 3 or play a Devil's Egg on my own site. The only "real" options for turn 3 was a Root Spider which is fantastic or a Pudge due to Tower ramp, however that requires 2 cards.
  • Bowman can be tutored by Common Sense as it's an Ordinary...though I don't see this happen too often, but the synergy is there
  • ...now for the big brain....
  • The Bowman can use his Ranged ability while occupying an Entangle Terrain!
  • Ranged is an ability that is not negatively effected by Immobile
  • If the Bowman is adjacent to an opponent's Avatar while in Entangle (because I'm entangling my opponent's minions too and I may be swarmed) then I can still hit the opponent's Avatar by tapping the Bowman
  • I can also Ranged minions that are stuck in the Entangle
  • With the Bowman being 3 power, I essentially play it like a mini-Battlemage. Let's say I play a Bowman on curve, turn 3. Turn 4 I swing onto my opponent's site. Even if I don't have Battlemage up in the opponent's face, I can still Entangle where the Bowman and other minions are to start chipping away for a minimum of 3 with Bowman
  • [[Belmotte Longbowmen]] + [[Gigantism]] is cracked
  • Bowman can Ranged into a Gnome Hollow
  • (still testing out quantities. As of now, 4 Bosk and 3 Bowman feel good but I may switch those numbers or go to 3 and 3 to test)


Also, the BIGGEST weakness of the deck is [[Dispel]] or [[Disenchant]] (as you'll see in my Video 3 which will be posted soon) and having minions on board will only help with absorbing or not taking damage if the squad has my back


-1 [[Overpower]], -3 [[Lightning Bolt]]

  • These utility cards were removed to make room for BoskyBoi and The BelmotteBoyz
  • The removed quantities for Overpower and Lightning Bolt are for testing purposes and not final...yet
  • It is a lot of splash damage removed from the deck however with the addition of minions, the potential for more damage over time (and less damage taken) with bodies has a higher ceiling


-1 [[Whirling Blades]]

  • I REALLY want the deck to be at 4 CMC and under (which is how I originally built the deck) but Blades potential is so high and an incredible finisher (which is how I used it 99% of the time...play the whole game with 4 sites, draw into Blades, then when opponent is on Death's Door, draw a site, tap and play it, and whirl around like a ballerina
  • Also with having more minions in the deck to speed up the opponent's clock and access to Blink, the Blades seem not as important versus other cards currently in the deck


-1 [[Philosopher's Stone]]

  • It's all about card value and what I rank higher than others
  • The removal of Uncle Phil is due to valuing minions more than the cost reduction of the Stone, as it rarely helped speed up the game...in the long run. Maybe I could get a free Overpower and 2 cost Grapple which is insane, but over the course of the game after a splash play like that (and removing a lot of cards from my hand), it seemed less valuable as I get to the late game


What I'm currently testing as of; 6/14/24


+2 [[Devil's Egg]] / -2 [[Torshammar Trinket]]

  • Devil's Egg cancels out an opp's [[Angel's Egg]]
  • Damage over time as I'm on opp's site majority of the game
  • Trinket can be awkward to cast over time
  • If Trinket is in my opener, I'll bottom the Trinket. I wouldn't bottom a Devil's Egg against most Avatars
  • Negative - Egg can be destroyed
  • Negative - Egg can also be awkward to cast as a 3 drop


+1 [[Amethyst Core]] & +1 [[Onyx Core]] / -2 [[Flanking Maneuver]]

  • I value the ramp higher than the forced movement and card draw with Flank
  • If Flank is in my opener, I would bottom it. I would instant keep either of the Cores


+2 [[Gnome Hollows]] / -2 [[Holy Ground]]

  • Gnome Hollow is fantastic at board control, especially since I play a minimal amount of sites
  • The obvious is that Gnome Hollow can be awkward for Battlemage. Typically if I have it in my opener, I play it on my home site, so I can "sit" in Hollow
  • If Gnome Hollow is my 4th site (as I typically only play 4 sites) it will be my "wing" site. (The site to the left or right of my home site) This can be tricky as your opponent's Avatar could make their way into Hollow and then you'd have to rely on Spider/Spider & Teleport/Bolt which isn't ideal but can be done
  • Holy Ground's life heal is great for early aggro, however I currently value the control of Gnome Hollow higher than the 3 life (This may/could change)

deckinfo.name: Fire/Earth Tempo Rush
deckinfo.primer:
Why Did I Make This Deck?

This deck started off as a passion project for [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] but quickly realized that it could compete competitively against other top ranked decks.



Why Does This Deck Perform Well?

This deck focuses on trying to remove your opponents minions using minions and sites that still provide a benefit to you and that you're opponent must deal with. Build up your mana base with defensive sites and then start using combinations of minions, deserts and magic damage to take out your opponents minions is key to winning with this deck. Start double drawing once you have 5-6 sites down depending on you're hand and if you got Philosopher's Stone. Once you're opponent starts using up all their cards is when you can go all in for aggression since they likely won't have enough minions or spells to keep up with your weaker guys and drawing 2 spells per tun with Sorcerer. Everything in the deck is cheap at 3 or under to be able to play those 2 spells per turn as well


Basic Damage Combos

  • Vile Imp + Desert = Kills 3 power minions for 2 mana and puts a minion on the board
  • Kobolds + Desert = Kills 3 power minions for 3 mana and puts a minion on the board
  • Wicked Witch + Desert = Kills 3 power minions for 4 mana and puts a minion that reduces damage on the board
  • Vile Imp + Dragonettes = Kills 3 power minions for 5 mana and puts 2 minions on the board
  • Firebolts + Desert = Kills 4 power minions for 2 mana but no minions on the board
  • Kobolds + Overpower = Kills 4 power minions for 4 mana and puts a minion on the board
  • Vile Imp + Vile Imp/Kobolds = Kills 4 power minions for 4/5 mana and puts 2 minions on the board
  • Firebolts + Dragonettes = Kills 4 power minions for 5 mana and puts a minion on the board
  • Wicked Witch + Vile Imp = Kills 4 power minions for 6 mana and puts 2 minions on the board
  • Firebolts + Vile Imp/Kobolds = Kills 5 power minions for 4/5 mana and puts a minion on the board
  • Wicked Witch + Firebolts = Kills 5 power minions for 6 mana and puts a minon on the board
  • Wicked Witch + Overpower = Trades with 6 power minions and kills 5 power minions for 5 mana


Using these damage combos to kill you're opponents minions, typically 3 or less power minions, lets you save your larger removal like [[Bury]] and [[Disintegrate]] for the bigger 5 power or greater minions. Most of these damage combos can also be used on the enemy avatar if they are close enough to be within range. [[Jihad]] allows you to play minions these damaging minions right on top of you're opponent. [[Divine Healing]] is in the deck incase you get bad draws and took lots of damage early on and couldn't remove you're opponents minions early.



Advanced Damage Combos

  • Jihad + Kobolds = Kills 3 power minions and puts a minion on the board
  • Jihad + Kobolds + Vile Imp = Kills 5 power minions and puts 2 minions on the board
  • Jihad + Kobolds + Overpower = Kills 5 power minions and puts a minion on the board
  • Wicked Witch + Blocking = Kills 4 power minions and keeps a minion on the board if it was less than 4 power
  • Wicked Witch + Vile Imp/Kobolds + Desert = Kills 5 power minions and puts a minion on the board


These damage combos are far more unlikely and typically cost too much mana to play all on the same turn so you typically want to have one of these cards already on the board or place minions or Jihad in a way that you can set up combos like these.

deckinfo.name: Mortals Strong Together
deckinfo.primer:
This is Version 2 of my Mortals Learning to Swim Deck


Current Edits are for a Tournament so if you see anything different that is why.


Deck aims to play out a lot of foot soldiers with [[Border militia]] and other mortals and pump up them with [[House Arn Bannerman]], [[Crusade]], and [[Ruler of Thul]]. Use [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] to mainly copy your Bannerman, you can use it to copy [[Captain Baldassare]] (currently not in deck) or your opponent's stuff. Use [[Call to War]] to get bannerman out of the deck or to get a [[Shield maidens]] to stop one damage lethal effects. At my local tournament I was able to get all three Shield maidens out on a gnome hollows and that completely gave me the win as my opponent could not deal the 4 damage to get the death blow.


The deck is all 4 cost and under besides [[Orb of Ba'al Berith]] as once you get to 4 mana just start tapping [[Sorcerer]] to draw 2 cards a turn. But I would consider playing the occasional site so you can try and get more than just 2 or 3 foot soldiers from [[Border Militia]]. [[Frontier Settlers]] (currently not in deck) will be a great tool for this. Or [[Land Surveyor]] (currently not in deck)


[[Adept Illusionist]] is a great card as you will always have two in the realm, and are great spellcasters for [[Sleep]], [[Pollimorph]], and [[Ice Lance]]. Just be mindful of their proximity to Orb.


[[Crown Prince]] is a great 3 power for 3 as unless your opponent goes out of their way to remove all of your other minions prince will always go back to hand when it dies. So trades are fine.


[[Sirian Templar]] like prince is a 3 power for 3. But Templar does not take any damage from commonly played cards like [[vile imp]], [[pudge butcher]], [[Dead of Night Demon]] (will see more play as stealth decks get better), [[Grim Reaper]], [[Headless Haunt]], [[Anui Undine]], [[Nimbus Jinn]], and [[Daperyll Vampire]]. There are more cards that won't take damage from.


Like in most decks [[Common Sense]] is in this deck uses it to get both finishers and threats.


[[Royal Bodyguard]] is just a good protector of your avatar and it has saved me a few times.


[[Overpower]] (currently not in deck) has starting to see a lot more play for good reason, it is 1 mana and lets you take a trade into your minion living and your opponent's minion not. Or it makes your 1 power minion trade with a 3 power minion. Getting in two extra damage can make the difference in a lot of games. Overall overpower is a great card. [[Gigantism]] is just a better overpower


[[Swan Maidens]] (currently not in deck) are a low cost answer to other airborne minions and because Bannerman is a nearby buff they will normally still get that buff when on the offensive.


[[Iceberg]]s will save you from [[drown]] from water decks, and [[Old Salt Anchorman]] (currently not in deck) will save you from [[Bury]].


This deck does not need to be a mortals deck as it is not using [[King of the Realm]], but I like theming. If you ever play against a King of the Realm you do just kind of lose

deckinfo.name: Sparkmage Aggro
deckinfo.primer:
Competitive version: Competitive Sparkmage (Love and THunder) | by @Metroidpikmin.


This deck runs limited number of uniques. This list is more of a causal list and aims to give players a good entry point into sparkmage. See my competitive list. But the goal is to have fun and embrace the lightning. The only unique I think is a must is Kythera Mechanism (but it can be substituted with lucky charms).


If you want to use cores, I would recommend using 1 or running [[mix aer]] or just add them both. Some additional uniques I would recommend but if you don't have are all the ones in the list but again the deck does not need them. AL added a lot of cards that can fill in those holes. [[Ring of Morrigan]] is one of if not the best card from AL if you have it run it.



The plan is to use [[Sparkmage]] offensively, using cantrips and other low cost spells to play 2-3 spells a turn letting Sparkmage deal 2-6 damage.


The key cards are [[teleport]], [[blink]] and [[Tactical Move]], the deck wins with sparkmage, and getting Sparkmage close without tapping so you can use that ability is key. [[Kythera Mechanism]] is the best card in the whole deck, let's just get that straight. Sparkmage, [[Lightning Bolt]], [[Thunderstorm]], [[Headless Haunt]], all have the word random Mechanism puts in a lot of work, letting you hit what you want to hit. There are a couple of other notable cards, [[poisonous dagger]] lets Sparkmage kill any minion letting you deal with 5 plus power minions easily. [[Highland Princess]] grabs Mechanism or a core. Really all of the cards serve a purpose. With all the cards except the artifacts and a few others, all other cards being two air threshold puts a lot of work in. [[Gyre Hippogriffs]] are a great 4 drop as if you can use the Sparkmage ability for 4 mana you can deal 5 damage. They are also great for closing out a match



[[Devil's egg]] after you teleport to your opponent's sites cast it into your hand. Dont forget to drop it if you have to retreat


This deck is aggro, but not the win turn 3 or 4 kind of aggro. This is an aggressive deck once you have a mana you teleport near your opponent and start zapping them for 2-6 a turn. You can win fast but the deck wants to get to 4 to 6 mana quickly, so getting an [[Imperial Road]] (currently not in deck) or just one of the Cores if you run them will go a long way in the deck. Then from there get close, cast spells to build up the threshold, and tap for damage. I love casting teleport, then 2 lightning bolts and tapping to deal 4 with Sparkmage, if all of that hits the opponent's avatar you just did 10 damage in one turn.


Try to place the stall sites, [[Free City]] [[Mountain Pass]] [[Perilous Bridge]] [[Great Wall]] [[Dome of Osiros]], these all by you time until you can draw some movement spells. And don't be afraid to retreat with [[Cloud City]] or a [[Teleport]] if it keeps you alive longer, the [[Angel's Egg]] (currently in sideboard) can do a lot


All of the minions in the deck are to help you keep pressure and let you deal 2 with [[Sparkmage]]. Even the card [[Phantasmal Shade]] (not in deck currently) which most people would look at as say that is its bad, as it dies to anything that strikes it, is great in the deck, for 3 mana I get a 4 power minion and I can deal 2 with Sparkmage. It is really good. 


I took out Shade and a mix for four copies of [[Cloud Spirit]] it is a great minion in Sparkmage. It is a great blocker with its Movement + 2. It is two threshold so that is 2 damage when cast. it is easy to get two out in a single turn.


[[Chaos Twister]] and [[Raise Dead]] are also great options.


[[Wind Slyph]] is back off the table seems like Sparkmage got an FAQ update, his ability tracks spells the player has cast not what Sparkmage has cast.

[[Orb of Ba'al Berith]] now also doubles your air threshold count for sparkmage's ability. It can be tricky to play with as you might be up in your opponents face, but if you have a wind slyph just use her. Or if you can keep you Sparkmage in the middle you can keep the orb in the middle

deckinfo.name: Chapel Perilous
deckinfo.primer:
In Arthurian Legend, seekers of the Grail must try to enter the Chapel Perilous, where their virtue and sanity are tested. A trial apart from all others—the only way out is through, but will your faith in this deck still be intact when your knights face impossible odds?


Welcome to Sorcery's first 4 color Money Pile. The name of the game is play sweet unique knights as fast as you can building on the back row until you can just absolutely overwhelm the Realm with the full power of the Round Table and the artifacts in it's war chest.





***05/26/25 MAJOR UPDATE***


It's BACK! So after an extremely long 6 months of playing this as my side project pet deck in the predominantly Archimago Control /Druid Midrange/Sorcerer Aggro meta — I have made a LOT of changes. The following Chapel Perilous list can go toe-to-toe with most decks in the meta, but I won't lie to you, aggro is very hard. A good pilot knows it's a race, and they will win it every single time. I should probably find a way to shove in pebbled paths tbh. Maybe in another 6 months! Also you don't tend to encounter a ton of Bower of Bliss out there anymore — but boy howdy is it a wild time when you do lol.


Ok so we've had to substantially alter the magic and artifact package, and honestly should have been playing shatter strike and earthquake from the jump. They are very very good. But here it is:


OUT


-4 Cores (They were only relevant as early game ramp. We traded some of that explosiveness for spells that will give us a chance against the wider meta)

-2 Valor (this card is actually just bad)

-1 Dispel (making room for shatter strike)

-1 Sir Agravaine (never impacted the board in a powerful enough way)

-2 Rescue (amazing with a specific handful of knights and royalty but too much of a corner case card)

-1 Pendragon Legacy (this was largely in the deck to remove targets from deathspeaker have replaced with Feast of Crows for now)



IN


+2 Shatter Strike

+ 2 Earthquake

+2 Lightning Bolt

+3 Blink

+ 1 Feast of Crows

+ 1 Cave-In


And that's the update! I'm going to try to get back to getting some serious reps in with this deck and will update as I can. Your mulligan is still the most important choice you will make playing this deck. To make the threshold work, you HAVE to aggressively mull to try and hit a tournament ground or a 3/4 element site nothing has changed about that.


~ Hardhope


Previous Updates




*11/09/24 Minor UPDATE:


leap attack and sir bors the younger removed and replaced with 3x war horse after it's showing at sorcerycon.


*10/23/24 Minor UPDATE:


Swapping out 3x duel to try 2x leap attack, adding Ring of Morrigan. It's simple too powerful to not try.



*10/21/24 MAJOR UPDATE:


Forgot to hit save the first time... so here goes again.


If you've played it, you already know that the deck is good. If you can stabilize and overwhelm the realm with knights, you will have the adv in most match ups. AoA and Battlemage are still very difficult match ups. Any kind of fast aggro is going to punish a midrange shell like this. That's just part of playing in a healthy meta. That said there are some cards that will HOSE this deck that are within our power to play around. So we have to evolve to combat them.


First up: The Green Knight is out, King of the Realm is in. We can only sustain one tripple threshold card and it has to be this one IMO. Many of you have asked, and after testing I can confirm that having all of your knights suddenly pledge fealty to an opposing king will make you want to vomit. Strategically, hold your KotR until it will put victory into your hands, or sandbag it if you think your opponent is likely to have one.


Ok. Next up is Duel. It's not the best, but with all the water stuff happening right now bury just doesn't feel good. If you have suggestions let me know in the comments — duel does not feel long for this decklist, but I haven't settled on it's replacement yet.


Next, some quick theory on flex slots. They are: Excalibur, The Round Table, Ruler of Thule, Sir Bedivere, and Sir Bors the Younger. If you want to run Ring of Morrigan, go for it. It probably should be an auto include in most decks. I'm just not ready to try it yet.


ok now for the really big changes.


Atlas Deck: Removing 1 Aquaduct, 1 Lighthouse, 1 Steppe, 1 Ruins. Adding 1 Pristine Paradise, 2 Crossroads, and most importantly, 1 Smokestack of Gnaak.


Digging for tournament grounds and whatever threshhold you need to it with crossroads is a game changer. Furthermore crossroads are going to dig for smokestacks a huge percentage of the time so let's break down why.


Smokestacks. THIS CARD. It turns off all the downsides to Pristine Paradise, Avalon, Colour out of Space, the back row tri elemental sites, ect. It also combats Roots, and even more importantly, Bower of Bliss, which every faire and druid deck are going to be running for the rest of the year. Smokestacks is vital to making this deck viable.


and last but not least...


Mulligans: Use all of your mull cards sculpting sites. You really don't want to keep a hand that doesn't have a 3 or 4 threshold site in it, or a tournament grounds, which is the card that makes the whole deck work.


Wedding hall will win you more games than you think. Wild I know.



*10/6/24 UPDATE: Removed Tom Thumb (not enough overall synergy.) Removed Lady Iseult (just trying stuff) and removed the two copies of Tactical Move in favor of trying out what things feel like running 4 copies of Duel since our knights are generally favorably positioned with higher toughness to win, and to see if it helps enable us to pick fights to get deathrite triggers when we want them. Sites currently feel balanced, but crossroads may be necessary to increase consistency.

Avalon is great, but it realllly sucks giving certain opposing Avatars the free threshold.

deckinfo.name: Waveshaper Tempo
deckinfo.primer:
NOW UPDATED FOR AL AND 50/30 (finally ... )


The Waveshaper brings water to the metagame in a big way! All of a sudden, we can play [[Anui Undine]] and [[Pirate Ship]] and reliably attack using our Avatar ability, but we also get a sweet bonus of tapping down enemies!


This deck is designed to get to 5 or 6 sites and then use the Waveshaper ability most turns to tap down relevant enemies, flood sites tactically, and clear / create the path for your powerful minions.


There's harder removal in the form of [[Drown]] and [[Atlantean Fate]], the [[Riptide]] combos with [[Troll Bridge]] to take out enemy minions.


The [[Plague of Frogs]], [[Adept Illusionist]], [[Tadpole Pool]] combine with [[Pnakotic Manuscript]] for some more card advantage.


There's power, trickery and synergy in this deck to reward the tactical pilot and counter lots of popular decks in the metagame.


Lots of little things all add up to give you flexibility. [[Coy Nixie]] can reposition enemies onto your Troll Bridges and into other dangerous locations. [[Giant Shark]] and [[Riptide]] gives you more removal options or ways to chew up an enemy avatar for big damage, [[Ruler of Thul]] gives you some sneaky ways to finish the game or get minions in interesting positions, and [[Maelstrom]] works so well with Waveshaper, pulling enemy minions into a single location for you to tap them down.


The air spells allow for some additional tactical flexibility and help finish off the game once you get the opponent to Death's Door.


[[Blink]] lets you move your submerged minions (e.g. Anui) from defensive to offensive positions in the subsurface so you can launch an attack.

deckinfo.name: 1st Blue Moon Cornerstone: Exceptionally Sligh
deckinfo.primer:
Hello,


**UPDATED DECK LIST**

https://curiosa.io/decks/cmjau0q4f57qozrfmy5yh22kc


﻿*** Deck is Obsolete because of Gothic and [[Druid]] nerf.***


This is my exceptional mono fire deck! The goal of this list is to put early pressure on the opponent with efficient minions, eke out card advantage where we can, and hopefully land a killing blow with a lucky burn spell.


We are aiming for a consistent and efficient early game. That is why the curve is low and does not include a lot of big finishers like [[Panorama Manticore]]. That is also why we are sticking with one element and not running Steam Druid. A big benefit of being mono fire is we get to run fun utility lands for extra value! 

  • [[Town]]: early ramp, a lot of the minions are exceptional and town will smooth out your early game.
  • [[Sinkhole]]: Removes problems like [[Pebbled Paths]] or [[Perilous Bridge]]. 
  • [[Wizards Den]]: Free card advantage-ish!!
  • [[Rift Valley]]: Sometimes deals with problematic sites, sometimes a free movement spell.

7 to 8 colorless sites seems to be the sweet spot if you consistently want to get (F)(F) early.



Mulligans 

Spells:

  • Mulligan all magic spells (except [[Pact with the devil]]... maybe), we want minions for early pressure.
  • Mulligan any finishers namely [[Rebecks]] & [[Boudicca]].
  • Remember what magic and finishers you mulligan, as they will not be outs later!!
  • Always keep [[Torshammer Trinket]].
  • Always keep [[Jihad]].
  • Don't clog your opening spells with lots of 4 drops if you don't have [[Town]].

Sites:

If your hand has a good curve of minions you can be very aggressive with Site.

  • If you are playing against control or earth dig for [[Sinkhole]] or [[smokestacks]].
  • [[River of Flame]] is one of the few answers to [[Root Spider]].
  • If your not playing against [[Archimago]] you can mulligan [[Funeral Pyre]].
  • If your not playing against [[Druid]] you can mulligan [[Arid Desert]].
  • [[Forge]] is strong in your opening hand, but you only need 1. 
  • If your opening hand is 3 (F)sites mulligan 1 or 2 unimportant ones in hopes of Hitting [[Town]] or [[Sinkhole]]. 
  • [[Town]] is super strong in your opening. 
  • Always mulligan [[Wizard Den]].
  • Its often poor to keep both [[Town]] and [[Sinkhole]], you will need (F)(F) early, use best judgment.


Game Play

Don't be afraid to play a [[Vile Imp]] or [[ Clamor of Harpies]] for no value. Its okay if [[Quarrelsome Kolbolds]] has to hit your [[Druid]] for 2, there is value in keeping up tempo and keeping your opponent under pressure. In that vain sometimes its okay to throw a [[Minor Explosion]] at the opposing avatar in the name of mana efficiency. Keep the games short and limit your opponents options. While the deck can play the value / control game (and sometimes you have to), we will often lose the late / long game.


It is usually correct to draw from your spell book. Only draw from your atlas if you can not make a play or REALLY need to double spell in a turn.


You can be pretty aggressive moving and attacking with your Avatar. You can double spell most the deck with 6 or 7 sites, so don't be afraid to skip a site draw or placement if you can get good value off it. Don't flip [[Druid]] unless it buys you a turn preventing a killing blow. Most of the time Tawny is more valuable.


"If you can be one thing, you should be efficient."




--------------------------------------------------------


Top 4 @ SCG Con Baltimore: Crossroads!

10-26-25


Notes from Baltimore:

  • [[Blaze]] under preformed. Low impact and bad against a flipped [[Druid]].
  • [[Clamor of Harpies]] plays well with [[Jihad]].
  • [[Clamor of Harpies]] teleport ability is mandatory, meaning you must move your tawny if there are no other legal targets.
  • [[Hillock Basilisk]] was amazing, and will 100% of the time cause a judge to be called.
  • [[Peasant Revolt]] was under whelming, buuuttttt seems important. (could be sooo good)
  • Super weak to an early [[ring of morrigan]] may want to run [[Shatter strike]].
  • The Atlas was great, all the utility site did work! And was never short on threshold!
  • [[Town]] is an MVP, can't stress this enough
  • this deck crushes other [[Druid]] decks especially steam :-)
  • using [[Clamor of Harpies]] to teleport a [[War Horse]] carrying a [[Siege Giant]], then having the [[Siege Giant]] throw the [[War Horse]] along with himself is my dream.
  • I had so much fun, and everyone I played against was so nice <3


1st Place @ Blue Moon Games: Cornerstone!

11-2-25


﻿Changes:

-1 [[Rebecks]] +1 [[Hillock Basilisk]]

-1 [[Blaze]] +1 [[Minor Explosion]]


Wanted to get a 2nd copy of [[Hillock Basilisk]] in, [[Rebecks]] was okay but coasting 5 and dying to [[Peasant Revolt]] seemed like a fine cut. [[Blaze]] underwhelmed just added another [[Minor Explosion]] because Druid is everywhere.


Notes from Blue Moon:

  • [[Hillock Basilisk]] continues to impress. profitably trading into another 3 power minion is great. or killing a 5 power minion with a lil [[vile imp]] help. Continues his streak of judges being being called 2 for 2.
  • [[Peasant Revolt]] actually blew up 3 sites in the finals against Steam Druid and is a nice safety blanket to have against a lot of top end minions and [[Drums of Doom]]. (it was sooo good!)
  • [[Archimago]] was banned for this event so I cut [[Funeral Pyre]] for [[Poisoned Well]].
  • [[Monstrous Lion]] is becoming a little situational, I usually just use him as removal, its weird throwing him down just to chase an avatar. may cut one and add [[Rebecks]] back in I seldom double spell on 4 anyway. Honestly [[Monstrous Lion]] and [[Hillock Basilisk]] kind of fill the same role I could totally see making that swap.
  • With so many Steam Druids running around [[Rift Valley]] hasn't been super useful, but Idk what site I would add in it place.
  • [[Vile Imp]] is the unsung hero of this deck just a beauty, so good lol
  • Played both my team mates in rounds 1 and 2, SO SORRY!!
  • The event was a blast, Met some cool people! (had a fun draft afterwards)
  • Still did not get to live the dream :(

deckinfo.primer:
Overview


The strategy is pretty straightforward: overwhelm your opponent in the early game with Earth's overstatted minions and then carry your advantage through the mid game with [[Avatar of Air]]'s mobility and Air's powerful magics.

Even without any Charge minions this deck hits hard and very fast, punishing any slow start or bricky hand from the opponent. Most of my games at the tournament were over before my opponent could manage to do anything meaningful.

Playing the deck requires good fundamentals of the game, especially site and minion placing, and being able to always plan a couple turns ahead with your avatar position.

The main way this deck loses is by being to greedy at the mulligan and bricking on threshold, so try to aim for a smooth hand that has a turn 2 and turn 3 play rather than hyperfocusing on getting a [[Pudge Butcher]] out on turn 3.



Tips and Tricks


Having a good grasp of some of the common play patterns of this deck can help better understand some of the building choices so I decided to include some tips on how to sequence and place your cards better.


-At the cost of sounding too obvious: ALWAYS place an Air site on turn 1, waste a Tower if you have to.

-One of the strongest plays of the deck is to play a double threshold site on turn 1, followed by an Earth site and a Tower to play a 4 drop on turn 3. This is obviously only possible if you open a double threshold site, so don't try to gamble for it.

-Try to to place your Air sites in a V shape, this way you have access to [[Avatar of Air]]'s ability in as many rows and columns as possible. This is especially important to be able to move again your [[Pudge Butcher]] if needed.

-In the early game it's usually best to cast your minions on top of you so you can fling them the following turn where they are most needed. Later in the game the choice isn't as obvious because you might need your minions in different positions to be able to block and you want to be able to fling [[Avatar of Air]] itself or to move it and fling something else if needed.

-After you have developed your sites you can start attacking with your avatar, especially if your opponent also has Air sites.

-If you're able to, try to space your non-Ordinary sites to make [[Atlantean Fate]] as bad as possible.



Card Choices


Artifacts

-[[Ring of Morrigan]]: this deck doesn't abuse it as much as others because you're casting only 1 spell each turn most of the time, however [[Avatar of Air]]'s mobility means you can always hit something meaningful with it and it's a great tool to deal the lethal blow.

-[[Grim Guisarme]]: playing a lot of high-statted minions means this card hits extra hard giving less time to the opponent and making healing often ineffective. You can also occasionaly combo it with [[Grapple Shot]] on the avatar for a surprise OTK.

-[[Rolling Boulder]]: I was originally playing 2 but after noticing that the deck can sometimes struggle against a wide board of small minions I decided to run the full set. It's fine to roll it once and just leave it there but I generally try to have it end up in a spot within reach so that my opponent has to play around it and most importantly can't steal it.


Minions

-[[Bosk Troll]]: the deck really wants to have a turn 2 play and this is the best option after [[Kettletop Leprechaun]].

-[[Kettletop Leprechaun]]: the best 2 drop available, being able to draw spell instead of site more often really helps offsetting the lack of draw power.

-[[Autumn Unicorn]]: an overstatted drop with no draw back is all the decks really wants, the double threshold can sometimes be tricky to handle but it's still worth playing it over the other options.

-[[Headless Haunt]]: same as [[Autumn Unicorn]] except having an Air threshold allows you to keep some hands where you cast it on turn 2 you otherwise would be forced to mulligan. During testing I was convinced the random teleport gave you a good result on average, but at the tournament I was particularly unlucky with the dice so I'm considering [[Belmotte Longbowmen]] as a replacement.

-[[Shield Maidens]]: I was initally not sold on playing an understatted minion in a deck that just wants to overwhelm the opponent with raw stats but after testing it became undeniable that this card gives excellent support against almost every matchup, even against decks that don't run [[Poison Nova]].

-[[Sir Bors the Younger]]: I already liked the card on its own but being able to move it around for free just makes it busted, having only 2 health is generally irrelevant.

-[[Dalcean Phalanx]]: once again an overstatted minion with an hardly relevant drawback.

-[[Pudge Butcher]]: the star of the deck, it's already strong outside of it but combining it with [[Avatar of Air]] makes it almost unstoppable and forces your opponent to keep feeding it minions to not get their avatar dragged.

-[[Sir Perceval]]: mostly a filler card since I wanted one more 4 drop, if you get it out very early you can force a situation where your opponent can't stop it from reaching its site but most of the time don't bother trying to get the draw.

-[[Daperyll Vampire]]: after the rules changes this card is just too good to not be played in every Air deck that reaches 5 mana.

-[[Sir Galahad]]: meant to be the 4th [[Daperyll Vampire]] but hasn't been amazing so far, could very well be replaced by a [[Hounds of Ondaros]].

-[[Riddle Sphinx]]: in my opinion one of the most underrated cards in the game right now. At worst it's a 4 power flyer that cycles itself, at best you have mulliganed at the bottom an impactful late game card like [[Earthquake]] or [[Whirling Blades]] and can trick your opponent into letting you draw it instead of a random card. It's been really helpful in squeezing out a little bit of extra gas in longer games.


Magics

-[[Browse]]: mostly a filler card but the threshold isn't very hard to get and it can help you find the right card to kill your opponent or deal with a tricky board. It can also set up the bottom for [[Riddle Sphinx]].

-[[Common Sense]]: while it's a tempo loss, being able to have extra copies of [[Dispel]], [[Bury]] and [[Grapple Shot]] in the deck without risking to brick on them is worth the 2 extra mana you have to spend. Getting a minion with it doesn't come up often.

-[[Dispel]]: it just feels necessary to run at least 1 to deal with [[Ring of Morrigan]], [[Jihad]], [[Atlantean Fate]] and other pesky cards.

-[[Bury]]: a spot removal that can double as artifact hate, it's true that there is a lot of Water going around recently but it hasn't been a problem yet.

-[[Grapple Shot]]: one of the best Air cards in the game, espacially in a deck full of high-statted minions like this. I realized at the time of writing this primer that I didn't draw a single copy during the tournament.

-[[Earthquake]]: as I said before for [[Rolling Boulder]] I wanted some ways to deal with wide boards, moving the sites around can also be very beneficial since the deck is very focused on positioning.

-[[Whirling Blades]]: it was initally at 2 copies because I feared bricking on it but I found it to be one of the best cards in the deck. It clears wide boards with no regards for Stealth, can increase your damage to end games faster and it's a great tool to deal the fatal blow.


Sites

You want to play as many Air sites as possible while keeping high enough chances to have 2 Earth sites by turn 4. I initially took the ratios from other topping [[Avatar of Air]] lists, then tweaked them a little because I found the deck can afford to run a low number of no-threshold sites and there are a couple I think are strong enough to justify the risk.


-[[Glastonbury Tor]], [[The Colour Out of Space]], [[Tintagel]], [[Valley of Delight]], [[Windmill]]: this deck simply can't work without running as many multi-element sites as possible, so to not lose to [[Atlantean Fate]] too hard you need to compensate by not playing many others non-Ordinary sites. Thankfully the deck doesn't really benefit from most of them anyway so it's not a big loss.

-[[Dark Tower]], [[Gothic Tower]], [[Lone Tower]]: they allow some of the strongest plays in your deck but can end up being wasted because of threshold so I don't play more copies, don't be greedy during the mulligan and get rid of them if you can't arrange a meaningful play without risking to brick on threshold.

-[[Hunter's Lodge]]: I don't think I've resolved its ability once during testing or at the tournament but the potential to counter [[Infiltrate]], [[Sir Agravaine]] and [[Morgana le Fay]] seems more valuable than a Foot Soldier.

-[[Lookout]]: I think the info on the opponent's hand is a little overrated but since I wanted an Air site to play on turn 1 if I don't get a multi-element one this is the only Ordinary option.

-[[Pebbled Paths]]: Charge is the strongest keyword in the game, so of course you wanna play the site that shuts it down.

-[[Pillar of Zeiros]]: it's often just an Earth site that does nothing but it's always good to have extra insurance against an aggro deck randomly opening nuts and running you down too fast.

-[[Wizard's Den]]: similar to [[Riddle Sphinx]] the extra card can be the difference between a won game and one that gets stolen right under your nose, being the aggressor in most matchups and emptying your hand generally quickly means you won't have to worry too much about having to discard a spell because of it.

-[[Sinkhole]]: the strongest site in the deck, why nobody else is playing it is beyond me. You can't be greedy with it in the mulligan but if you open an hand that allows you to use it on turn 2 or 3 while playing on curve you just automatically win. It can also help in the [[Archimago]] matchup by freeing the way from [[Gnome Hollows]] and [[Perilous Bridge]] or by messing with their threshold.



What's not here and why


-[[Onyx Core]]: while increasing your chances of reaching double Earth threshold is good and all, risking to draw a site when you need a spell in a deck that is already struggling with card draw isn't worth it.

-[[Torshammar Trinket]]: one of the most recent exclusions from the deck, the extra power was often not relevant enough and I was running too many cards that are dead if I don't already have a minion on the board.

-[[Blink]], [[Flanking Maneuver]] and other mobility cards: since this deck is heavily focused on tempo I don't want to use extra mana to do something my avatar does for free, with the exception of [[Headless Haunt]] I rarely find myself in spots where they would be useful.

-[[Crusade]]: the deck does run a lot of Earth minion but the extra power is often overkill and the minions in this deck don't really benefit from being summoned on your opponent's side of the board.

-[[Highland Falconer]], [[Palliburrie Bats]]: playing these or [[Bosk Troll]] is mostly a meta call, right now there are too many [[Vile Imp]] and [[Quarrelsome Kobolds]] around so I prefer having a single stronger minion. Deck space is also an issue.

-[[Highland Princess]]: an auto-inclusion if you're running [[Torshammar Trinket]] but not worth playing it with only 1 target in the deck.

-[[Hyter Sprites]]: could be another replacement for [[Bosk Troll]] to combo with [[Lookout]], I didn't have time to test it.

-[[Lightning Bolt]], [[Magic Missiles]]: the deck usually just runs over small creatures and doesn't need help in dealing the fatal blow.

-[[Belmotte Longbowmen]]: a possible replacement for [[Headless Haunt]], but has the big downside of being very reliant on [[Avatar of Air]] to be effective.

-[[Castle Haunt]]: might look fine on paper but not being able to move is a terrible drawback in practice.

-[[Feast for Crows]]: a strong effect but it's not worth the tempo loss and card disadvantage.

-[[Root Spider]]: the deck doesn't really need to worry about defending itself, playing them on the surface and then flinging them on an enemy an burrowing them can be a cool play tho.

-[[Chaos Twister]]: it should probably be in the deck over some combination of [[Earthquake]]/[[Rolling Boulder]]/[[Whirling Blades]], I just despise the mechanic and refuse to spend time to learn how to blow it consistently.

-[[Gigantism]]: it's a 3rd copy of [[Grim Guisarme]] that costs 1 mana more, didn't seem needed and increases the amount of cards that require a minion on the board to be relevant. (Please note that I'm biased by the fact that I kept drawing it when my opponent was already in DD during testing)

-[[Mask of Mayhem]]: not being able to control which minion attacks and when is too big of a drawback.

-[[Royal Bodyguard]]: the effect isn't needed often and I didn't need other 4 drops but it could replace [[Sir Perceval]].

-[[The Black Plague]]: ends up being just a clunky removal, the deck doesn't struggle against [[Root Spider]] enough to justify it.

-[[Hounds of Ondaros]]: I've seen a lot of people say this card is amazing but I have never tested it and I don't really see where the hype is, if you're not really sold on [[Riddle Sphinx]] (but you should be) this is the obvious replacement.

-[[Bower of Bliss]]: this is one of the other no-threshold sites I find powerful enought to play in your atlas, unfortunately that would mean giving up on [[Shield Maidens]] which is just too important.

-[[Cloud City]]: moving it around rarely accomplishes something so I'd rather play more ordinary sites.

-[[Common Village]], [[Humble Village]], [[Rustic Village]], [[Simple Village]]: they can be run over [[Hunter's Lodge]] but you can't play them on turn 1 and would rather use all your mana on the following turns.

-[[Kingdom of Agartha]]: turning off all your removals isn't worth it.

-[[Merlin's Tower]]: This deck only plays a couple of Magics and they're mostly situational so it's hard to arrange plays with it, better to just play more Ordinary sites instead.

-[[Mirror Realm]]: there aren't many strong sites to copy in the deck.

-[[Perilous Bridge]]: this site ends up being a problem for yourself more often than it is for your opponent, you generally would want to place it right in front of your avatar but that's where you usually need an Earth site.

-[[Rift Valley]]: the positional advantage isn't worth running a non-Ordinary site.



Tournament Report


Round 1 vs [[Deathspeaker]]: W

He tried his best to stall with [[Grain Sparrow]] and [[Bane Widow]] but ended up bricking on double [[Poison Nova]] against my [[Shield Maidens]].


Round 2 vs Earth Water Fire [[Sorcerer]]: W

It was an original build based around Mortals. A slow starting hand put him on the backfoot and then [[Whirling Blades]] killing [[Sir Agravaine]], [[Kingswood Poachers]] and [[Shield Maidens]] sealed the deal.


Round 3 vs Steam [[Druid]]: W

The game was single handedly won by turn 1 [[Ring of Morrigan]] completely shutting down Tawny. A well timed [[Sinkhole]] also helped in keeping him on the defensive.


Round 4 vs Fire Air [[Pathfinder]]: W

She hard bricked on threshold, I'm pretty sure the only spell she managed to cast for the entire game was a single [[Hamlet's Ablaze!]] right before losing.


Round 5 vs Mono FIre [[Druid]]: ID

We were both guaranteed in top so we decided to rest for a round and go get some coffee. I ended up being 1st in Swiss since both my round 3 and 4 opponent's made top cut.


Top 8 vs Air Earth [[Druid]]: W

I had a shaky start because I struggled to find a 2nd Earth site but my opponent bricked harder. He kept an heavy Air hand hoping to draw a 2nd Air site but didn't draw it until very late after I already hit the first one with [[Sinkhole]].


Top 4 vs [[Archimago]]: L

It's already a very hard matchup for the deck on average hands, but my opponent just made it impossible by opening [[Ring of Morrigan]], double [[Divine Healing]] and then drawing plenty of removal while I didn't see the cards I need most. Fortunately it was piloted by my best friend and testing partner @Solaris who ended up winning the whole thing so I didn't feel too bad about it.

deckinfo.name: 1st Place Cornerstone Gothenburg - Waveshaper Control
deckinfo.primer:
Waveshaper has been my go-to avatar since I started playing with the precons. The amount of control the tap ability provides and room for interesting plays with cards that synergies with the body of water makes every game feel fresh and unique.


Strategy

This is a control deck that aims to survive the first rounds with hindering sites ([[Perilous Bridge]], [[Tadpole Pool]], [[Troll Bridge]], [[Babbling Brook]]) and sticky minions. ([[Adept Illusionist]], [[Sir Tom Thumb]], [[Lugbog Cat]])


We accrue value with [[Highland Princess]], [[Grandmaster Wizard]] and [[Captain Baldassare]]. There are multiple ways to recast and regain these effects through [[Selfsame Simulacrum]], [[Fey Changeling]] and [[The Lady of the Lake]]. To make sure we are staying ahead in resources over our opponent we have [[Atlantean Fate]], [[The Great Drowning of Men]] and [[Wrath of the Sea]].


To get our opponent to death’s door we utilize evasive and hard to kill minions such as [[Gyre Hippogriffs]], [[Daperyll Vampire]], [[Hounds of Ondaros]], [[Questing Beast]], [[Mester Stoor Worm]], [[The Green Knight]] and [[Thundering Giant]].


Other Notable Cards

  • [[Plague of Frogs]] - Gum up the board (and potentially get a big life total swing together with [[Ruler of Thul]].
  • [[Pollimorph]] & [[Mesmerism]] - Remove/turn any pesky minions.
  • [[Stormy Seas]] - Submerge artifacts that give our opponent an edge or remove one or multiple minions.
  • [[Riptide]] - We can use it on our minions to protect them if we need to overextend, pull our enemies' minions or avatar to get to them or pull them aside to get an attack we otherwise couldn’t get through.
  • [[Watchtower]] & [[Hounds of Ondaros]] - Stealth is a very strong mechanic and we use these to being able to remove [[Infiltrate]] and letting us target [[Morgana le Fay]].


Highland Princess Jewel Box

The suite of artifacts are specifically chosen for the Highland Princess and the impact they can provide for the game. Depending when you play her and what other cards you have in hand/play, the decision can turn the game in your favor.  

  • [[Amethyst Core]] & [[Aquamarine Core]] - Stable choices to secure the threshold you need.
  • [[Mix Aer]] - Usually used to get a Grandmaster Wizard into play.
  • [[Ring of Morrigan]] & [[Torshammar Trinket]] - Great against aggressive decks when you need to make sure you can kill their minions without trading with your own.
  • [[Philosopher’s Stone]] - Great for the mid- and end-game when you would like to cast multiple spells.

deckinfo.name: Dragonlord-Xeraphine Konrul (Cornerstone Oulu 2025, 2-2)
deckinfo.primer:
The deck went 2-2 in Swiss in a 17-player Cornerstone event.


Game 1: Druid (fire/water). A quick 0-2 loss, not much I could achieve here.


Game 2: Druid (water/air). Lost game 1, but was able to squeeze a 2-1 victory with some good draws.


Game 3: Pathfinder (fire/air). Again, lost game 1, but won 2-1 in the end by getting to high mana and rotating strong uniques from the cemetery.


Game 4: Druid (water). Lost 0-2 in long, grindy matches. The opponent had lots of submerge effects, so I tried to dig for Icebergs, but failed. Maybe they could have turned one of the games. But there would have been no time for a game 3 so perhaps it was for the best.


Top 8: Druid (water/fire). Quickly lost 0-2. Pretty similar to the first match of the day. Steam Druid is just too fast and my deck had very limited ways to deal with a flipped Druid with Drums.


Conclusions:


Xeraphine takes a bit of time to get going, but if you are able to draw a strong unique (Morgana, Boudicca, etc) and play it over and over again, the deck can be very strong.


The key is to build the manabase up to 6-7 without delay. Then find a beefy unique. Play new minions instead of activating Xeraphine and only use left over mana for her ability. Remember that she also gives your Avatar flying which can be handy at times.


The three Drowns are a meta choice to submerge Drums from a flipped Druid, not meant for creature removal.


When sideboarding Autumn Rivers replace Icebergs if opponent doesn’t play water. The Drowns can be kept for creature removal or swapped for Shatter Strikes when not facing a Druid.


Warp Spasm is a pet card due to art. Another card would probably be better. The main deck Xeraphine Konryl should possibly also be a different card. And forgot to add 2x Ashkelon Phoenix to sidebord.


In casual play the deck is fun and does well againts most Avatars. In a tournament where 4/5 of my games were against Druids, the 2-2 finish was perhaps a bit overperforming.

deckinfo.primer:
round 1, 2-0 win vs druid

round 2, 1-1 draw vs pathfinder

round 3, 0-2 loss vs druid

round 4, 2-1 win vs druid


This is about the best air/fire Battlemage I can come up with to go against the current meta of Druids. Druid still feels like a tough match-up but I don't think there is much I can do about it. While the deck can be played with both aggro and control gameplan depending on the match-up a Druid deck that goes for the early aggression is too fast to keep up with. More midrangey Druid is perhaps bit more manageable but requires at least some luck to win.


I think that against Archimago the success of this deck comes down to if they can find and cast a Divine Healing or not. Once they play their first Divine Healing it is very difficult to race them but if they don't find one then I should have a reasonable chance to win. My experience is very limited however and the results could be very different against differently built Archis.


Rest of the avatars I don't have even nearly enough experience. Pathfinder probably has the edge especially if they're playing some site destruction. Avatar of Air also seems like a struggle. I've had reasonable success against Enchantress but the deck has gone from almost burn to this more control style of deck so I might not be fast enough. At least I have 3 Disenchants on the sideboard for the games 2 and 3 if I lose the first game.


At the moment the only improvements I will be doing are to replace the two copies of Bottomless Pit and the single copy of The Colour Out of Space with something else. COOS is not needed. The thresholds are fairly easy to meet when I will play 5+ sites in a game. Deserts, a third Beacon and third Lookout are among my top picks for those slots.
