deckinfo.name: 8-0 cornerstone elementalist
deckinfo.primer:
This deck has a primary goal of casting a 4 drop on turn 2 and on turn 3 by using the artifacts and towers/camelot.

Most 4 drops outclass the majority of minions available to the opponent at this stage in the game putting high pressure on their premium removal as most spells don't deal with a pudge butcher on a water site on turn 2 before it gets to do it's thing.


Particularly interesting start is the cloud city, mirror realm and amethyst core opener, on the play you can site lock the opponent to a maximum of 3 sites, though more frequently it will merely act as a counter to polar explorers/ruler of thuul and provide a mobile gun platform for your pudge butcher's and sir bors the younger.


The elementalist benefits greatly from the threshold it gets if you convert it into speed therefore in late game situations is crucial to have more card draw than your opponent as their secondary ability is likely to give them a source of card advantage. Luckily being able to play the major card draw cards from all colours should mean that you run more premium draw effects than your opponent.


Lastly a plethora of boardwipes is essential to make your card draw and recursion swing the game in your favor, especially a fields of camlann into resurrecting a grand master wizard with lady of the lake can really turn the tide of a game.


This version is pre dragonlord as i did not have access to the cards


Hope this helps

deckinfo.primer:
This enchantress deck placed 2nd at the Invercargill New Zealand, Cornerstone 2025


TBA - Dunedin New Zealand, Cornerstone 2025.

Overall theme of this deck is competitive Enchantress, to try and hit your opponent as quick as you can with your animated Auras.


Mulligans - Spells - You really want to aim for at least one Aura in hand and a cheap spell to activate aura, if you draw into multiple cores then that is fine but be sure to use them early and draw from spells rather than sites because Aura is key!!. The more expensive Auras can be difficult to get out early game so an Aura with a lower mana cost is ideal.

Sites - Threshold can be difficult to meet especially with the big Auras so ideally you want the Double threshold sites or Colour out of Space. Best to Mulligan single threshold sites if you can to try and get to multi-threshold sites.

deckinfo.name: GenCon 2025 Crossroads 6th Place, 6-1 (E/F Sorcerer 55/31)
deckinfo.primer:
Ideally, you want an aggressive or low to the ground start with some sort of card advantage. If you have multiple 4 cost minions in hand pitch them and dive deeper for more aggression and value.


Infiltrate is usually a snap keep in opener along with kettletops, imps and other aggro pieces under 4 mana. Slumbering giants is also a keeper but I will usually hold a desert to play on turn 4 if I don't have another way to wake her. From there get to 5 sites and start double drawing spells until you need the additional mana to outvalue the opponent by casting 2 spells per turn.


Don't get greedy with board presence if you have control, play this like a midrange build that has the capacity to go aggressive. Don't be afraid to sandbag spells you don't necessarily need to play and always be aware of Atlantean fate when moving around onto your sites. The ordinary sites in the deck will naturally help with this, but still be aware of wide area removal as it will almost always happen eventually. Just do your best to minimize risk.


Thanks for checking this out, I hope this helps!

deckinfo.name: Zoo-Lander - 2nd place Wintercup of Wonders
deckinfo.primer:
This Zoo deck is designed to play optimal cards by leveraging the mana and threshold curve effectively.

The deck curve peaks at 7 sites, but most plays can be done efficiently with just 5-6 sites.


General Strategy

The deck belongs to the "midrange" archetype, meaning that can be played either as an aggressive deck or a control deck, depending on the match-up ("MU").

The main strategy revolves around drawing from your spellbook every turn while deploying resilient and "bulky" minions. Indeed, the special ability of [[Geomancer]] allows you to land at least 5 sites without drawing from your atlas.


Minions are employed to:

  1. destroy opponent's minions through aggressive clashes.
  2. deal significant damage to the opponent’s avatar.


Spells support this strategy by:

  • Removing threats or resources from the opponent ([[bury]], [[earthquake]], [[dispel]]).
  • Enhancing board presence and increasing the minions' range of action ([[blink]], [[grapple shot]]).

[[Lightning bolt]] serves as either removal or a finisher, while [[Common sense]] improves deck consistency by tutoring the right answers for specific scenarios (e.g., [[Lightning bolt]], [[dispel]], [[amazon warriors]], and sideboard cards).


Match-Up Strategies

Vs [[ARCHIMAGO]]

Focus on destroying its artifacts to slow down its plays, while playing as many minions as possible to aggressively attack opponent's sites.

Although [[Archimago]] has a decent number of removal spells (including board clears like [[poison nova]] and [[earthquake]]), they are usually not enough to answer every threat without interrupting the development of its own game plan.

Its sites ([[gnome hollows]], [[perilous bridge]]) can be annoying, but the deck’s mobility tools ([[blink]], [[grapple shot]]) and site control cards ([[atlas wanderers]], [[earthquake]]) help overcome these obstacles.

It is crucial to pressure the avatar immediately by dealing damage and moving units onto its sites.


Vs FURY ROAD/[[SORCERER]] AGGRO


The key is to maintain a strong board presence by summoning minions and attacking whenever possible.

In the early game, [[Sorcerer]] may deal a considerable amount of damage, but by the time you reach 4-5 sites, your larger minions should be able to handle the aggression effectively.

Alternatively, if you’re on the play, you can adopt a more aggressive approach and race for damage. Generally, [[Sorcerer]] struggles to control the board, being unable to winning the damage race.

Useful sites to disrupt its strategy include [[pebbled path]] and [[sinkhole]].


Vs [[DRUID]]



Vs [[ENCHANTRESS]]

[[Enchantress]] is a control deck with little to no early game presence.

While its auras can efficiently remove units, their high cost leaves opportunities for an aggressive strategy. Be aware that entering the late game could be problematic.


Vs [[DEATHSPEAKER]]

This is a combo-control deck that draws heavily to execute a [[Nimbus Jinn]] finisher.

  • [[Root spider]] counters its combo effectively.
  • It plays interaction and numerous board clears—remain cautious.
  • The deck has a low curve, so expect early plays to stall your aggression.

Vs [[AVATAR OF AIR]]

An aggressive deck using airborne and voidwalk units, relying on sites that hinder ground movement.

  • It focuses on artifacts to boost its units.
  • Plays with only 3-4 sites, meaning interaction is limited.
  • Primarily aims for a fast damage race.

Due to [[Avatar of Air]]’s mobility, delivering a final blow can be tricky when it’s near death. Watch out for [[rolling boulder]].

Vs [[BATTLEMAGE]]

[[Battlemage]] features a fast curve and aggressive early turns.

  • It uses a variety of "shrink" spells to weaken your units.
  • High mobility allows it to reposition aggressively, often employing [[grapple shot]] to approach your avatar in the first few turns.


SIDE DECK

  • 3x [[just a rock]]: helpful against the majority of the decks currently in the meta, in particular against [[Battlemage]] (even though recent lists run a lower amount of artifacts),[[Archimago]] (especially against [[ring of morrigan]], [[philosopher stone]] and [[angel's egg]], note that it doesn't work against [[orb of ba'al berith]]) and maybe [[Druid]] for [[drums of doom]]
  • 2x [[divine healing]]: it is basically against fury road and other kinds of [[sorcerer]] aggros, it helps you to survive few more turns while you establish board presence with your minions.
  • 2 x [[shield maidens]]: generally against [[archimago]] and decks that fire a lot of projectiles. Still have to find its proper role as a side card.
  • 2 x [[lightning bolt]]: against aggro decks and decks that tend to flood the board with small minions.
  • 1 x [[disenchant]]: again against decks that widely employ artifacts ([[Battlemage]], [[Archimago]]) but also against [[Enchantress]] and water decks (against [[atlantean fate]] and [[mariner's curse]]).


Changes History

24.12.2024

  • Removed: 1 [[Summoning Sphere]], 2 [[Craterize]]
  • Added: 2 [[Wyvern]], 1 [[Blink]]

F / W / a Steam Mage

Elements: Fire, Water, Air

Event Information

This deck took 5th place in the Columbus Ohio Explorer Series. Where Archimago and Ring of Morrigan were banned.


It's an update version of this deck:

https://curiosa.io/decks/cm3iwz25l0018bpm7ka2yh6bq

Which took 2nd place at a 20 player event in Detroit in late 2024.


The deck went 5-0 before top cut, where I lost in the first round to the same player playing a variant of the same deck that the previous iteration lost to in the finals of Detroit (before explorer series). I also played him in the Chicago explorer series event. Every game has been a nail biter where we have doored each other, and where every game I had the win on the following turn. In anticipation of playing against that exact deck I added troll bridges and a free city for this event. This is because I know in that matchup he is the aggressor, and having one turn to stabilize could mean the difference.


The Game Plan:


Build an efficient early game board using fetch minions, playing slightly defensively. Move to opponents side using movement tech like [[Ruler of Thul]] or [[Polar Explores]] to circumvent defensive sites for large amount of damage in one turn.


Heavy damage: [[Ruler of Thul]], [[Sir Agravaine]]

Enablers: [[Polar Explorers]]

The Final Blow: [[Magic Missiles]], [[Lightning Bolt]]

deckinfo.primer:
Pathfinder is probably the riskiest avatar to run, especially when considering the atlas draw. That said it can offer the most explosiveness..potentially landing 6 sites while drawing 6 cards.


This deck hopes for at least 2 of the first 4 sites to be fire, otherwise you won't get enough speed to win.


MULLIGAN EVERYTHING EXCEPT.

  1. Ring of Morrigan.
  2. Ruby Core
  3. Jihad
  4. Boudicca.

Against Archimago do not mulligan Courtesan Thais.

Against Sorcerer keep Warhorse.


Playing.

It's a race....decimate before you are decimated.


Block only if you are losing the race.

Attack sights wherever profitable. Trade attack when you have more minions.

If your opponent allows Pathfinder to get upfield early, do so.

Save your blinks for when you really need a site or to get adjacent to an enemy avatar on deaths door.

Late game airborne minions should be used like chess pieces to contain the enemy avatar.

Don't play cerebrus if there are more aggressive options.


Card selection


I didn't put 2 monstrous lions because I wanted to be able to attack sites, nothing worse than a monstrous lion without any food.

I only have 1 manticore and 1 infernal legion ( which explains the phoenix and ancient dragon).

Shackles are great Against big minions...but the deck was fire / earth for a while, and really I was worried about missing bury.

There is only one siege giant because I wanted immolation and major explosion ( for protection and late game victory).

Pellinore is explosiveness, kill a big minion and draw a card??

Coutesan is to be played against Archimago as soon as you see craterize in the graveyard or thier hand ( via lookout ).

regarding sites, i wanted pillar of Z, but i left it in buffalo and didn't have it with me.

Also I like randomness!


My experience.

Gen con was my first time playing in an actual event. The community of players and organizers were fantastic. That was the biggest takeaway.

Technically tho.

Game 1, I drew 3 of 4 air sites and lost convincingly. The sight that shuts of charge minions was a major kryptonite.


I drew good sites games 2-7, and fortunately did not run into any avatars who disrupted my site placement which guaranteed me 6 or more sites in the early going.

Manticore hit the table once.

I drew ancient dragon 3x but never played it. There were some close calls , but I think this deck has decent chance against druid, deathspeaker is a favorable match up as well (as the deck has almost zero genesis minions). I was fortunate to not run into battlemage, archimago OR any heavy water decks.

I had alot of fun and in truth I got lucky catching the right card in a few close matches.


I have a small 5-6 person play group just south of Buffalo NY, that meets up at kitchen tables. The closest gamestore to carry it is 90 minutes away. This game is great, I hope it grow legs and thrives..Can't wait for gothic.!!

deckinfo.primer:
Playstyle: Midrange with a bit of combo

Difficulty: 5/10


This deck is essentially a collection of two-card combos built on top of a solid midrange core that makes excellent use of Tawny.


Core Combos:

  • Tawny + Trinkets/Desserts – This enables efficient trades in the early game.
  • Ring of Morrigan + Trinkets – In the right matchup, this combo can be game-breaking and provides an almost unfair advantage.
  • Sir Agravaine + Frogs/Tawny – You can eliminate nearly any threat or bring your opponent’s Avatar to deathsdoor, as each Frog will deal 3 damage when attacking adjacent to Agravaine.
  • Boudicca + Frogs/Tawny – Similar to Agravaine, playing Boudicca right after casting Plague of Frogs can be devastating.
  • Ruler of Thul + Frogs – This was strong in Alpha and remains so.
  • Manuscript + Frogs – Another combo that was effective in Alpha and still holds up.
  • Pact with the Devil + Tawny – This synergy is amazing, but be mindful of the potential tempo loss.
  • Snowball + Frogs/Tawny – Once you Frogball, you never go back! 😆

Beast Package:

The Beast package is quite fun—it rarely makes a significant impact, but having a potential Lugbog Cat on turn 2 can be huge.


Card Choices:


A lot of the card choices are debatable and come down to personal preference. Generally, water minions have a harder time making the cut compared to fire minions due to Jihad.

While many Druid lists run Drums of Doom, I personally see it as more of a trap. If you’ve reached a point where its effect is beneficial, you’re already behind. I’d rather have a card that helps maintain pressure.


Sites:


Since the deck’s range is quite extreme and demanding, I don’t play a single site that doesn’t provide Threshold. So far, I’ve never had an issue reaching the required Threshold, but I also mulligan aggressively for dual/triple lands.

deckinfo.name: Path in Flames (2nd Place @ Singapore Parti Lansio)
deckinfo.primer:
Greetings, fellow sorcerers!


Thanks for taking the time to read this primer.

In conjunction with the release of Arthurian Legends, a Constructed tournament was held on 7th October 2024 in Singapore. (Shoutout to Woon Jiun & Ya Qiong for organizing the fun event!)

The tournament uses the older deckbuilding rules -- minimum 40 spells + 20 sites.

Total of 4 rounds swiss, with each round being Best of 1 with a time limit of 1 hour.

Arthurian Legends cards are legal for use at the Constructed tournament.


This deck was inspired by two main sources:

  1. The "Warpath" deck by @DREW (https://curiosa.io/decks/cln6yls630004mn0gwla6q957)
  2. Playtest sessions at Gamersaurus Rex (Shoutout to Malcolm Soh & Japheth!)


Playstyle & Game Plan

This deck plays as a midrange deck that focuses on board control & high threat density.

Generally, the deck relies on Pathfinder to hit land drops every turn, so it is not uncommon for the deck to have 6 or more sites on the grid.

To take advantage of the large amounts of mana, the spell deck is packed with cards with high card quality.

This includes minion with high threat quality (Petrosian Cavalry/Panorama Manticore) & board control elements (Root Spider/Vile Imp/Pudge Butcher/Death Dealer).

Once your minions put the opponent at death's door, you can use projectiles or damage spells to close the game (Firebolts/Flame Wave/Craterize).


The deck is pretty versatile in adjusting its game plan when needed.

Against aggro decks, you can compete against them by prioritizing cheaper minions & removals (mulligan anything that costs 5 or more!).

Against other midrange/control decks, deploy your minions patiently to exhaust opponent's removals & board wipes, before taking control with the larger creatures (Panorama Manticore/Ancient Dragon/Death Dealer) & damage spells (Firebolts/Flame Wave/Craterize).


You will enjoy this deck if

  • You enjoy casting large and powerful spells
  • You enjoy playing a difficult-to-pilot deck
  • You like trapping your opponents with placement of minions (Pudge Butcher/Panorama Manticore/Ancient Dragon), damage spells & Jihad
  • You like a deck with late-game inevitability


Key Cards

Vile Imps: Efficient way of removing opponent's minions in the early game to make sure you can reach Turn 5, after which your board wipes and larger minions can take over.


Root Spiders: Countless primers have espoused the usefulness of the spider. Disabling opponent's best threats until you find a removal/board wipe is hard to ignore.


Pudge Butcher: Versatile card that limits the movement choices for opposing minions and Avatars. One of the best cards in the deck.


Bury: Effective removal.


Infiltrate: Taking control of enemy minions to close out the game can be unexpected for many opponents.


Fail-Not Bow: New card from Arthurian Legends that turn any minion you have into a fearsome threat. Sometimes you can win out of nowhere if the opponent runs far away only to be hit by a minion equipped with bow.


Earthquake: Extremely essential. On hindsight, I would have played another copy in place of a Royal Bodyguard.


Flame Wave: Flame Wave excels in wiping the board clean and also closing out games when the opponent is at death's door.


Briar Patch: This new site from Arthurian Legends makes it awkward for opposing minions to chase your Avatar.


Gnome Hollows/Free City: Both of these sites allow Pathfinder to seek refuge from larger threats and stall the game until you draw your board wipes.


Pillar of Zeiros: Important site for life gain and also stopping Deathspeaker decks from going ham with the cemetery.


Funeral Pyre: The new Arthurian Legends site is an additional site against opposing Deathspeaker decks.


Combos

The deck does not have any infinite combos. However, there are some synergies that are worth highlighting.


Panorama Manticore + Fail-Not Bow: Manticore with Bow can allow you to kill every minion on the board


Secret Tunnel + Root Spider: This classic "combo" allows you to traverse to most sites (depending on the placement of your sites) and stun enemy minions.


That's all for now! Will try to create a 50 card version soon!

deckinfo.primer:
Kythera Mechanism: The ability to control my Haunt’s location and keep my opponent’s Haunts stuck in the void or dying in a Bottomless Pit in the mirror match was too good of an idea to pass up. If it ever mattered, I'd be able to determine my opponent’s lightning bolts if I had to choose between one of my minions and my AoA.


No Lightning Bolts for me? Yea... I was conflicted about that. Looking back, bye-bye Land Deeds, hello Lightning Bolts!


Sling Pixies: The MVP. Airborne + Ranged is a nasty combo. No wonder the design team only granted the Pixies with 1 power. As a fan of beefy minions, I never understood the significance of those little, early game pings until I played AoA. The goal is to create enough of a disparity in life total that your opponent feels like they're on their back foot by Turn 4 or 5; and while they continue to try and stabilize, you're still dropping minions, or Devil's Eggs and Madd. Bells to make their life even more miserable. Pixies can just hang out and ping the enemy with an undefendable strike every turn; it's Airborne makes it invulnerable to ground minions (without the help of additional spells); and with 3 Trinkets in the deck, it has the potential to deal up to 4 damage in one Ranged strike.

Against Roots, Pixies are FANTASTIC blockers against the opponent’s Amazon Warriors post-Root detonation. Post-Roots, the opponent's got 5-mana and casts Warriors. On our turn, we’ve got 1-mana, drop Pixies and block for days until we stabilize.




Splashing for Fire:

Smokestacks was already in the Atlas to turn off Roots or a Cloud City in the mirror match. My question became, how much more fire affinity can I add to the Atlas without detracting from my Air affinity while also providing enough Fire sites to run single-fire-threshold spells? The deck was already running Lighthouse, so swap those out for Ruins; that's 4 fire resources. Colour out of Space seemed so obvious for multiple reasons: 1. It provides Air and Fire, 2. It offers the same defensive capability as the Lighthouses (water sites) to ward off Root Spider, 3. AoA decks cap at 4 or 5 sites, so the chances of keeping Colour next to a void is pretty high; and in the extreme case I draw Colour and Smokestacks, Smokey just turns off Colour's limiting factor. Oh, and AoA can still treat it as an Air site to push things.

But what to remove? Every other site seemed so integral. As big of a fan boy as I am for Free City, one of the 3 copies had to go. Yes, they offer insane protection and can force your opponent to stall out while trying to figure out how to storm the castle. BUT, in a mirror match, Free City is lackluster being unable to attack enemy Airborne minions, AND it doesn't offer elemental affinity, so one copy had to go.


What fire spells are worth making the cut?

THIS was a tough question, but the end result (for better or worse) was a pair of Scarabs and a pair of Kobolds.


Sacred Scarabs: In my experience, fetching Scarabs with a Falconer feels like a total win until your opponent 2-for-1's you and removes both minions (it's happened more times than I care to admit). But in those situations, I wasn't piloting AoA. Simplest explanation: make sure AoA is on an Air site > cast Falconer on same site as AoA > fetch Scarab > use AoA to fly Scarabs to a nearby site where they won't grenade the home team for 3. Then your opponent has a much more difficult decision to make. If they stay on board until your next turn, ideally strap them with a Trinket or two, swing in, explode, and deal a total of 5 or 6 damage with Trinket(s) returning to your hand.


Quarrelsome Kobolds: Aggression. Aggression. Aggression. Cast them and push them as close to enemy unit as possible with AoA, then end the turn with a free, undefendable strike for 2 damage. Or is it 3 damage? Or 4, or 5? Because we're crazy enough to run 3 Trinkets. AoA loves its Gyre Hippos. Those Charging winged beasts feel so good to drop on turn 3 after a Dark Tower (my personal favorite Tower). From my pov, Kobolds are a 3-mana, 2-power minion with faux-Charge. If your opponent has played their sites aggressively enough to meet you in the middle of the board, ideally you've flown AoA to your forward most site on a previous turn > cast Kobolds on the same site as AoA > fly them straight ahead to bonk the enemy Avatar EOT who is probably still hanging out on their initial square.


Fire's Honorable Mentions: Blaze, Petrosian Cavalry, Pit Vipers, Wils-o-the-Wisp, Clamor of Harpies, Firebolts, Infiltrate and Poison Nova.


What did I learn after going 4-0 and then losing in the 5th and 6th round?

  • Land Deed wasn't worth it. I didn't get enough playtesting in to determine if I really wanted a pair of Land Deeds in there. However, in playtesting, I managed to get Madd Bells out by Turn 3 on the wings of a Bat and it caused such massive setbacks for my opponent it made me ask, "how can I make THAT more consistent?" Land Deed was the answer. In hindsight, I wish I could go back in time, slap me on the wrist and say "NO. Either you put the Bolts back in there or the Flanking Maneuver, but you are taking those Deeds out. Hell, put in a 4th Grapple Shot!"
  • In order to learn from my losses, it helps to remember the sequences that led to the loss. My Round 5 match against Zalem was brutal. By T3 he’d played (in this order): Free City, G Hollows, and Mirror Realm to copy Free City. The game was basically over; G Hollows locks out nearly 50% of my minions (Haunt, Phase Ass, Gyre Hippo and Dap Vamp); and Free City prevents me from attacking with 80% of my minions! For better or worse, I’m wired to never give up, so the game continued. I tried my best to attack his Hollows with my Bats and his Free Cities with my Haunts, until he dropped 2 Root Spiders by T4 and T5 under is Hollows. My only options at that point were to draw into a Smokestacks to shut down his FC and GH or put a Sling Pixies on his Free City and ping his Seer for 2 with Trinket. He Infiltrated my Bat on his third Hollow (the only one without a burrowed Root Spider) and used it to kill my Cloud Spirit attempting to enter the Hollows and join the meager assault. The most disheartening series of turns was when he cast a Scarecrow into the hands of Root Spider which prevented my burrowed Bat from entering and killing the Spider. The next turn he dropped 1 Angel’s Egg to the spider, and the turn after, a 2nd Angel’s Egg. In a matter of turns he'd completely inverted the life total. The entire game I never saw my Devil’s Eggs, Madd Bells or Boulders. All would’ve helped in their own way.
  • AoA benefits from splashing an element. Is Fire the best element to splash? I've been asking that since playtesting for GenCon. How I'd love to run Windmills for Earth, push my opponent's minions onto Air sites above my burrowed Root Spider, or Common Sense for a Grapple Shot or Bolt. Put the Lighthouses back in for Water and use Shrink help my small minions take out larger threats. But that's just one element (no pun intended) of the beauty of this game. There are so many options for creative answers. If I could go back, I would've put in 2 Pit Vipers, maybe 3, to handle enemy Root Spiders.
  • My Round 6 loss against Chris (I forget his last name) was pretty straightforward. He piloted AoE and ran me over with Earthquake and big minions. What can you say? Earth is good. Again, Pit Vipers would've been ideal, surviving Earthquake, and easily trading with any minion he put down. I don't recall drawing into my FC or BP which would've kept those ground minions at bay. Ultimately, I think I played my hand and the game in front of me the best I could. As the saying goes, you win some, you lose some.
  • Cheers!

deckinfo.name: Goon With the Wind - Courtesan Cup Day 1 - 6th Place
deckinfo.primer:
This is the Battlemage build I used to land in 6th place during constructed Swiss at the 2024 Courtesan Cup. Thanks to Potato Knight, Drewid, CJ, Anger Worm, GoldenEagle, and all the other League players who helped me pull this list together for the tournament!


A few notes on how to pilot the deck:


  • I've played competitively with Battlemage for about 8 months, and I think the avatar is strongest when unpredictable and well positioned to deliver a tempo swing. Another way of looking at this is: I don't start the game hoping to race onto the opponent's sites ASAP and start attacking, because it's much easier for Battlemage to win the race to Death's Door when minions deliver the first 50-75% of life loss, the opponent must choose between multiple potential defense points, and Battlemage takes the opponent to Death's Door faster than they were expecting. The avatar's capacity to attack for 3+ is more valuable to me than the avatar's ability to draw a card when attacking and killing a minion.


  • I usually build 3 sites on the back row and initially play minions onto water sites or void squares. Site play from that point on varies vs. the opponent.


  • This build has the capacity to disrupt your opponent's early-game plan and make them question what the right play is. You should be causing life loss from turn 2 or 3, forcing the opponent to choose between spending mana on removal or leaving a threat on the board. Try to play a 3-drop on turn 2 (ideally Headless Haunt); otherwise, hit them with a Lightning Bolt. If possible, play Thunderstorm or Hippogriffs on turn 3. If you can Sinkhole them on turn 4 while also putting another minion on the board, do it.


  • Use Thunderstorms, minions, and mobility spells to bottleneck your opponent's attack vectors while maximizing yours. If you get Imperial Road-ed, in almost every case you should NOT play a site. If you get Rift Valley'd, remember to stay focused on winning the race to Death's Door (you may not necessarily want to focus your attacks on the Valley, since your minion removal options are limited).


  • You can win games at 4 mana, so think carefully about what tapping the Battlemage for 5 would get you.


A few notes on Spells:


  • Haunt is a real workhorse, and with a Blink or Flanking Maneuver in hand, you have to roll really badly to lose out on a turn of using a Haunt. Combos best with Trinket, Sword, Flanking Maneuver, and Grapple Shot.


  • Lightning Bolts are meant to be used liberally to speed up your clock against the opposing avatar, but can also defend against early pressure and minions that add up quickly (Bosk Troll, Kobolds, Dragonettes, Cavalry, Hippogriffs, Phase Assassins).


  • Pirate Ship is incredibly annoying as a defender against most decks, a painful speedbump against offensive Avatars, and devastating if your opponent turns out to be playing water. Combos best with Sword, Grapple Shot, Floodplain, and Undertow.


  • Chaos Twister is last-resort removal, especially if you're playing in person. I rarely use Twister offensively and will mulligan in search of any other 3-drop or 4-drop Spell.


  • Windblast is a card to hold against Gnome Hollows and Root Spider threats, but can also put the opponent's avatar into position for an offensive Grapple Shot.


Most favorable matchups: Deathspeaker, Enchantress, Waveshaper


Least favorable matchups: Roots, Avatar of Air, Kythera Sorcerer

deckinfo.primer:
This is an updated version of the list I played in West Virginia to get 1st. In FL, I only lost twice, both to the same undefeated player, and both games we were both on Death's Door.

You can see a Dech Teck video for my West Virginia List here: https://youtu.be/oeG288eMsmA?si=zfLYX4qttLLmqFSJ

The main changes I made were adding more cores, P-Stone, another EP, and switching Browse for Pact with the Devil. Having all 3 EPs is big because it's such a strong card and having only 2 gives a decent chances you won't see it in a game. Pact with the Devil I chose over Browse because with Browse, I often found myself putting 6 good cards at the bottom of my deck, with Pact, I can sacrifice one of my many Spellcasters to draw 3, not only not putting cards at the bottom, but putting a Wizard in the cemetery to reuse with Deathspeaker and giving more fuel to Nimbus Jinn if needed.

deckinfo.primer:
Placed 7th @ CTCCQ on 4/6/24; loses came from 2nd & 3rd place decks.


Updates

Removed [[Aqueduct]] for [[Tadpole Pool]] - didn't use in the tournament, since I couldn't find it. 😅😂


Primer

  • [[Vril Revenant]] is used to apply some pressure on the opponent. Have to make sure its attack will hit or use it to get rid of a high power threat. Best used when you have a lot of mana to swing big.
  • [[Fey Changeling]] is used to get rid of [[Infiltrate]], or bounce any of our auras or other minions back to our hand to refuse them. Can also be used to show opponent down by a turn or more.
  • [[Selfsame Simulacrum]] is used to make an extra copy of any of our auras or copy a major threat the opponent has played. It’s a flex card in the deck.


Will try and get the deck down to 40 cards instead of 42 for consistency. Power difference when auras aren’t pulled is felt.

deckinfo.name: Community Day 1 - 3rd Place - George Deathspeaker (Air/Fire/Earth)
deckinfo.primer:
From George


This deck is my attempt to make Immortal Throne work (since I opened a foil one) and an excuse to go 3 color with all my expensive cards. You can use Deathspeaker’s ability to help using cards in graveyard to advance Immortal Throne.


Game plan

Ideally you fetch the Immortal Throne with dream quest and win off of it. The backup plan is to beat up your opponent with the creatures you have after killing all of theirs with your genesis abilities and magic spells.


Even if you don’t win with the Immortal Throne, most of the time you can still get great value out of it. Generally if I manage to play it I get around 4 card draws with it


Opening hand

Ideally you want a Core to start and you want at least a Land Surveyor or Vile Imp. For sites you just want thresholds that can support your opening hand. Ideally you get all 3 threshold for site, otherwise focus on fire and earth unless you have an apprentice wizard in hand since most of the early - mid game cards are earth/ fire


Early game

Get awesome value out of your cards and maintain board control/ not die too much early game. Get good trades with Vile Imp and Torshammar Trinket. 


Mid - late game

once you have enough mana you can go use your bigger creatures to beat them up and overwhelm them with your card advantage. If you already have a good board/ stabilized - try get card draws/ advance Immortal Throne so you can answer what your opponent play.


Good combos/ tips for some cards

Deathspeaker - Always keep in mind what you can play from your graveyard and also opponent’s graveyard. Remember this ability is free on death’s door. Sometimes if you need you, you can also send your genesis minions to die just to use it again. E.g Attack with vile imp and cast it from graveyard for 4 damage.


Immortal Throne - You would want to play this when you can activate at least 2 card draws preferably. So play it before your site and most of the time Torshammar Trinket would be your 1 cost trigger


Nimbus Jinn - when you have decent amount of cards in hand + summoning sphere you can summon this onto your opponent’s avatar and put them to death’s door


Clamor of Harpies - other than using this to get rid of your opponent’s small minions, you can also use this to move your own ones, and then buff them with Torshammar Trinket to get good trades


Summoning Sphere - You can use this with a lot of your genesis creature to do good damage. Vile Imp and Wraetannis Titan are the most notable ones.


Good cards to add

Good cards to include in this deck that I don’t have at the time - Earth Quake, Panorama Manticore, Death Dealer and Infiltrate. Some more dual sites will also be good. River of Flames would also be nice with some removal to help deal with burrowed creatures.


Weakness

This deck has some problems dealing with Root Spider and burrowing creatures. A few of the cards like Death Dealer and River of flames mentioned above will help with that. Vesuvius can also be used to help in a pinch.

If your opponent manage to take control in early - mid game it can be a little hard to come back unless you get off a good Poison Nova or Cave in. As mentioned, the cards in good cards to add will help with this.

hint.name: Community Day 1 - 2nd Place - Louis Sorcerer Aggro

deckinfo.name: Community Day 1 - 2nd Place - Louis Sorcerer Aggro
deckinfo.primer:
Hey I'm Louis,

I have a few ideas for decks and spitballed ideas. If requested enough I will make a Youtube video with a deck tech on my creations.


Current record

Event wins: 2

Wins: 12

Loss: 2

Draws: 0



Core Idea:

Main goal of this deck is to deploy as many dudes as possible and take them on a crusade, While also flying pudge around on zeppelins to take take on bigger threats.

Aggression and overwhelming swarms of units is how we plan to win. with blinks and lightning bolts as finishers.



Early game:

we aggressively mulligan for supporting minion units (Shield maiden's or a Pudge)

First 2-3 turns are focused on summoning as many Foot soldiers as we can early.

By turn 3-5 plan is to summon a shield maiden or a Bannerman to support our Foot Soldiers.

or place a pudge in line with the enemy avatar.

We want to encroach forward with our atlas placements trying to maximize our border with enemy atlas's as we can gain more units with Border militia.



Mid game:

Once you have a few forward minions and are going in for strikes on your opponents try to keep a foot soldier untapped near your supporting units to dive in front of the opponents minions (*note will not save them from ranged projectiles unless actually in front)

We need to time our removal to keep the aggression up. keeping tempo is very important in this deck.

Bury on a smaller unit to keep tempo can be okay for more avatar damage

Earthquake's and atlas Wanderers can change placements of atlas for better border militias and also to line up enemy avatar for pudge hook can be huge.


End Game:

Our way to keep up with large minions(anything with 4 or more power) and close out game is twofold:

I have an army:

  • border militia from our 6 copies (common sense can find one as needed)


I am unkillable:

  • Recursive threats in Crown prince and scourge zombies to keep up pressure.


Once you have got your opponent to death's door we have 3 main ways to close out games:

  • blinking a threat on top of the opponents avatar.
  • crusade of 100's of men surrounding avatar and exhausting defenders.
  • 3* copies of lightning bolt/grapple shot (2 common sense tutor for bolts/Grappels)



Things to keep in mind:

  • in a water matchup Bury, Cave in and Earthquake become much more defensive in nature due to lack of stable ground.


  • if you notice your opponent is playing desert atlas's try not to move foot soldiers forward turns 1-2 as you can lose them for free.


  • Remember our Werewolves have 2 ways to get them into play pay 3 mana OR sending a mortal (usually foot soldiers) to see god. This can trigger our zombies to return as well making 1 power man turn into a 2 power zombie(s) and a 3 power werewolf for no mana (have cut werewolves for now)


  • Keep one mortal in reserve for our crown prince he is very hard to deal with as a recursive threat but we need a servant class for him to rule over.


  • we only need 5 mana to cast everything in our deck and 7 to 8 to cast 2-3 spells a turn. after we have 5 to 6 atlas in play start drawing two cards a turn to gain card advantage.


If you liked this guide give me some feedback and if I reach enough likes I'll consider a Youtube video.


Cheers

deckinfo.primer:
The goal of the deck is to get the opponent to death's door as quickly as possible. Fast mana is not necessary early, but it can push you ahead faster. Getting a pudge or 5 drops early is key for pressure. Early pressure to get your opponent to death's door and late-game stabilization via sorcerer draws make this deck very potent. Defensive cards include pillar for deathdealer, Gnome hollows and free city for battlemage, avatar of Earth, ruler of Thule, and mirror matches, and quagmire for Pathfinder, AoE, and battlemage. Pudge on a free city will protect it from spiders.
